title: The tray rebuilds sync_guard() every 2 s, and that walks every retained ingest staging folder on the sync drive
where: companion/src/ccsync_companion/app.py:7749 (sync_guard -> ingest_staging_report app.py:8069) -> broll_ingest.py:3834-3839 (_dir_bytes broll_ingest.py:692); callers tray.py:3075 (_tray_snapshot, every 2.0 s) and reporter.py:1020
what: sync_guard() is the report section but the tray also calls it whole every 2 s. Its ingest_staging section recursively walks and stats every finished or held staging batch of both ingest kinds on every call. The staging root is inside local_root (<local_root>/Assets/B-roll Archive/.ingest and the music mount), batches are kept 7 days and held drops are never pruned. disk_snapshot() beside it is memoised for exactly the SYNC-2 reason; this walk is not.
cost: 43,200 tray calls/day plus 1,440-17,280 reporter calls/day, for 7 days after each drop (for ever for a held one). Three 100-clip drops = 1,500 files = 17 ms per call measured on local NVMe warm (~0.9% of a core on the tray thread plus ~0.35% on the reporter, beside Resolve); estimated 0.3-1 s per call over USB cold cache or SMB (base rig music staging has no override). If the drive goes ROOT_NOT_ANSWERING the walk blocks and both the tray refresh thread and the reporter thread park inside sync_guard(), so the machine stops reporting exactly when root_state=not_answering is what the dashboard needs (PLAUSIBLE, read not reproduced).
evidence: Read the chain app.py:7749/8069 -> broll_ingest.staging_report/_dir_bytes, broll_server.ingest_staging_root (broll_server.py:1649-1669), tray refresh loop (tray.py:5165, 5221-5258); no TTL and no root-state check. Probe: _dir_bytes over a synthetic 3-batch/1,500-file staging tree = 17.3 ms per call.
ledger: new (related: bug-comp-broll-4 held staging keeps the walk alive past retention)
fix: Memoise ingest_staging_report() like disk_snapshot() (TTL = dashboard_report_interval, floor 30 s), invalidate it from clear_finished_ingest_staging() and batch end/prune, and return the last value without touching disk while _root_state is not present; or keep a running byte count per staging entry in the ingestor. The space refusal (_space_refusal) keeps its exact walk at refusal time.

title: Two net use (+ subst) probes per media-tree tick when one is enough
where: companion/src/ccsync_companion/app.py:5210 then 5217 (_media_tree_loop); uncached p_mapping_mode() at app.py:5047; probe app.py:5383/5435 -> drive_swap.py:309-340
what: With Resolve open, each 120 s tick runs _classify_pool_once, whose p_mapping_mode() memo (10 s) expired a tick ago, so it spawns net use P: (and subst on subst-mapped rigs); seconds later _refresh_p_mapping_mode() spawns the identical probe again unconditionally.
cost: 720 ticks/day x 2 probes x 1-2 spawns = 1,440-2,880 spawns/day per Windows editor machine where 720-1,440 suffice; measured 13.4 ms (net use) + 12.6 ms (subst) per spawn, so ~19-38 s/day of spawn wall time, half redundant.
evidence: Loop order app.py:5208-5217 and the uncached call at app.py:5047; spawn timing probe.
fix: Call _refresh_p_mapping_mode() at the top of the tick before _refresh_media_tree_once(), or use p_mapping_mode_cached() in _classify_pool_once. Swaps must still invalidate the cache and the classification must still refuse while P: points at the server.

title: Seven workers share one try in start(); one raising silently skips the rest under the wrong name
what: proxy_generator, broll_ingestor, music_ingestor, job_runner and (since 2026-11-09) sorter_cards, sorter_volumes and ledger_outbox are started inside one try whose except logs 'failed to start the proxy generator', against the rule stated 25 lines below that each starter gets its own try.
cost: Any exception from an earlier starter (RuntimeError can't start new thread near the handle limit beside Resolve, a raising enabled property, a half-built object) leaves every later worker down for the life of the process with a log line naming the wrong component; none of them is supervised by LaneWatchdog. Trigger likelihood is low (PLAUSIBLE).
evidence: app.py:10620-10646 read; sorter starters added in f8102a4 / 06f033b.
fix: Move these seven into the existing (name, starter) tuple loop at app.py:10671 so each has its own try and its own name in the log. No happy-path change.

title: sync_guard() is 282 lines of 26 hand-written try blocks rebuilt in full by two threads; a table would allow per-section cadence
where: companion/src/ccsync_companion/app.py:7704-7985 (readers tray.py:3075, reporter.py:1020; blocked_report writes _blocked_since from both threads, app.py:8174-8179)
what: Every section is the same call/swallow/emit shape written out 26 times, citing 29 distinct bug ids. Being a monolith, every consumer pays for every section at its own rate: the tray rebuilds the whole report section every 2 s for a handful of keys, and an expensive section (comp-app-1) cannot get a slower cadence without another hand-written memo.
cost: 43,200 full rebuilds/day from the tray (two eula_accepted.json reads per tray tick counting the snapshot's own, two stall-file reads, stand-in ledger stats, the staging walk) for data the reporter already builds every 5-60 s; ~280 lines touched by every new report key.
evidence: AST/grep pass over app.py: __init__ 921 lines / 42 ids, sync_guard 282 / 29, _build_lanes 218 / 20.
fix: Express sections as a table of (key, getter, emit_when, ttl_seconds) with one isolating loop (about 150 lines saved, 'never raises' becomes structural), give walking/file-reading sections a TTL, and let the tray reuse the last built guard when it is younger than its tick. Keep the always-present sections always present and blocked computed last.

title: The manifest walk spends ~85% of its CPU building pathlib objects, on every machine, every 300 s
where: companion/src/ccsync_companion/manifest.py:186-226 (`Path(file_path).relative_to(project_dir)` and `rel.parts` per video file, `size_fn=os.path.getsize`), :369-373 (300 s loop)
what: For every video file the walk builds a `Path`, calls `relative_to` (which itself builds and compares several `Path`s), then `rel.parts` and `rel.as_posix()`, and stats the file a second time with `os.path.getsize`. The pathlib work, not the disk, is the cost. It runs whether or not a project is selected (rollup-only projects pay it too), on the manifest thread, holding the GIL against the tray, the reporter and the lanes.
cost: 50k files: 3.6 s of pure-Python CPU every 300 s on a local NVMe tree (1.2% of a core, all day, beside Resolve). At commercial scale (64 projects, 500k files on a base or wired rig) about 36 s per pass, 12% of a core, before any SMB latency. The second stat per file is a network round trip on an SMB `local_root`.
evidence: cProfile of one scan: 9.4 s profiled total, of which `pathlib.relative_to` 5.8 s cumulative (38,293 calls, 783k `PurePath.__getitem__`, 898k `Path.__init__`), `os.stat` via getsize 1.8 s. A rewrite with `os.scandir` recursion, a carried `"prefix/"` string, a carried in-Proxy flag and `DirEntry.stat()` (free on Windows) produced identical rollups for all 10 projects in 0.47 s best of 3 against 3.58 s (7.6x).
ledger: related to PL-RES-107 / prac-perf-3 (open: base rig walks the NAS, extra getsize). New here: the dominant cost is pathlib and it hits every machine, so the recorded fix (scandir + `entry.stat()`) alone leaves most of it in place.
fix: Walk with an explicit `os.scandir` stack carrying the relative prefix as a string and an `in_proxy` flag; size from `entry.stat().st_size`; `VIDEO_EXTS` as a frozenset. Must keep: the conflict-marker count ahead of the extension filter, the NFC fold only for comparison, the bytes-on-disk rel that is returned, the present-before-and-after check in `refresh_once`, and `size_fn` as a test seam (make `entry.stat` the default and accept an override).
risk: low risk (output pinned by the existing manifest tests; the probe shows equal rollups).

title: An unchanged manifest is still re-sent in full every 10 minutes, and one changed project re-sends all of them
what: Suppression is all-or-nothing per section: `local_manifest` is one sha1, so a new file in one ticked project re-sends every ticked project's per-file lists, and the server DELETEs and re-INSERTs all of them. And even with nothing changed, the forced 600 s resend ships the whole section again so the server can re-learn what it already holds.
cost: An editor with 10 ticked projects of ~5k files: the heavy body is 3.55 MB (measured) and the server rewrites ~40k `editor_media` rows, 0.27 s of write locks on desktop NVMe (27 ms per project; a NAS is slower). Idle, that is 144 resends a day: about 510 MB a day of upload per machine and ~5.8M row writes a day, every one of them a no-op. At 20 machines: ~10 GB/day into the dashboard and ~115M no-op row writes/day, all retained by the hourly ZFS snapshots (res-time-scale-10). While one project is syncing, the 300 s rescan changes the section and the other nine are rewritten with it.
evidence: `probe_manifest.py` (3.55 MB body for 10 selected projects, 16.8 MB for 64); `probe_server_write.py` (10 x 4,000-row `replace_editor_media` = 0.27 s, WAL grew 4.7 MB); code read of `_drop_unchanged_sections` (`(now - sent[1]) >= SECTION_RESEND_SECONDS` re-sends regardless of digest).
ledger: related to CR-62 (open: "the per-project change signal"), res-time-scale-10 and PL-RES-44 (open, gzip). The quantified cost of the forced resend and the keep-alive alternative below are new.
fix: Keep digests per project key (and per media-tree project), send only the changed keys (the server already treats an absent key as "leave it alone"). Replace the forced full resend with a keep-alive: send `{rel: digest}` for unchanged projects; the server bumps `refreshed_at` / `reported_at` with one UPDATE when its stored digest matches and answers `resend: [rels]` when it does not (restored backup, pruned rows, truncation). Must keep: the 14-day age-out still sees live machines (the keep-alive touches the timestamps), a failed POST suppresses nothing, a new editor identity clears the state.
effort: M effort (both sides of the wire, additive field, dashboard first)

title: Once `_fit_payload` has trimmed the manifest, it is never suppressed again: rebuilt, shed and re-sent every heavy tick, with a WARNING every minute
where: companion/src/ccsync_companion/reporter.py:1177-1183 (compares the digest of the UNFITTED section), :1199-1206 (`_note_sections_sent` stores the digest of the FITTED section), :1259-1262 (the WARNING)
what: `_drop_unchanged_sections` runs before fitting and hashes the full manifest; `_note_sections_sent` runs after the POST and hashes the trimmed one. When the body is over budget the two never match, so the unchanged-section suppression (CR-62, ops-efficiency-1) is permanently off for exactly the machines with the biggest manifests. Fitting is deterministic, so the same input always yields the same trimmed output; nothing is gained by re-sending it.
cost: An editor with 30 ticked projects of >=2,000 files (8.5 MB untrimmed): every 60 s the reporter serialises ~8.5-18 MB twice (digest, then fit), trims, sends, and logs `report payload is 8.5 MB (budget 7.3 MB): dropped the per-file lists ...` at WARNING. 60-140 ms of CPU and a transient multi-MB string per minute, 1,440 identical WARNING lines a day pushing the useful lines out of the rotated `companion.log` a support session reads, and 30-64 `editor_media_project` upserts a minute on the dashboard instead of one round every 10 minutes.
evidence: `probe_suppress.py`: three heavy posts of an unchanged manifest. 10 projects (2.8 MB, under budget): sent, omitted, omitted (CPU 58, 11, 11 ms). 30 projects: sent, sent, sent, each 4,925 bytes after trimming, CPU 82, 60, 61 ms, WARNING each time. 64 projects: sent x3, 141, 141, 137 ms.
ledger: new (a hole in CR-62's fix; KNOWN_BUGS states the fitted digest is recorded on purpose but not this consequence).
fix: Record both digests on acceptance (`(unfitted, fitted, at)`) and suppress when the new unfitted digest equals the stored unfitted one; keep the fitted one only for the "shed means not sent" rule. Log the budget WARNING on a change of the shed set, DEBUG otherwise. Must keep: a shed section still counts as not sent; a server-truncated reply still clears the state.

title: One byte over the budget strips the per-file lists from EVERY ticked project, not just enough of them
what: Step 1 sets `originals`/`proxies` to None on every project in one go and only then re-measures. The manifest is already in priority order (ticked, then most recently touched), so dropping lists from the tail until the body fits would keep the file lists of the projects that matter. Instead a machine that crosses 7 MiB by one project loses all of its per-file presence at once.
cost: An editor ticks a 26th project of >=2,000 files (body ~7.4 MB). From the next heavy report every project goes rollup-only. On the dashboard, `replace_editor_media` is no longer called for any of them, so their `editor_media` rows freeze at the last full report and are deleted by the 14-day age-out (db.py:10807-10809), after which the per-file sync view for that machine has nothing for any project, not just the new one. The editor did nothing but tick one more project.
evidence: `probe_suppress.py`: 30 projects at 8.5 MB -> `dropped the per-file lists from 30 project(s)`, final body 4,925 bytes against a 7.3 MB budget (99.9% of the budget unused). Dashboard path read at api.py:11388-11391 (lists only replaced when not None).
ledger: new; related to res-time-scale-4 (open, per-project 2000-file cap) and B6.
fix: In step 1 drop lists from the lowest-priority projects first (iterate the manifest in reverse order, re-measure every few projects or by subtracting each project's encoded size), stopping as soon as the body fits. Must keep: copies, never in-place edits of the cache's dicts; `truncated: True` on every project that lost its list; the later shedding steps unchanged.

title: A changed heavy section is serialised three times per report
where: companion/src/ccsync_companion/reporter.py:360-371 (`_section_digest`, sort_keys), :1177 (digest before fitting), :1236 (`_fit_payload` encode), :1202 (digest again after the POST)
what: Each heavy tick with a changed manifest JSON-encodes it once with `sort_keys` to digest it, once to measure and send it, and once more with `sort_keys` to record what was accepted. When nothing was trimmed the third digest is identical to the first. And on every idle heavy tick (60 s) the unchanged manifest is still re-encoded once just to discover it is unchanged, although `ManifestCache` knows whether it rescanned.
cost: 10 projects: 8 + 11 + 8 ms; 64 projects: 59 + 55 + 59 ms plus transient copies of a 16 MB string; the idle digest is 8-59 ms a minute per machine. Small, but it is on the reporter thread on the base rig, which also runs the encoder and the indexer.
evidence: `probe_manifest.py` timings (encode 11 / 55 ms, digest 8 / 59 ms for 10 / 64 projects).
ledger: new (COMP-CORE-5 of 2026-08-14 removed the fourth serialisation; these three remain).
fix: Reuse the pre-fit digest in `_note_sections_sent` when the section came through `_fit_payload` untouched; give `ManifestCache` (and the media-tree cache) a generation counter so an unchanged generation skips the digest entirely. Must keep: digest of the fitted content when it was trimmed (or the two-digest rule of comp-core-3).

title: On macOS the idle probe spawns `ioreg` on every report tick, uncached
confidence: PLAUSIBLE (not measurable on this Windows rig)
where: companion/src/ccsync_companion/idle.py:213-260 (`default_ioreg_run`, no cache); capabilities.py:317 and :383 (`idle_seconds` recomputed on every build, cached assembly or not); app.py:2396 / 2485 / 7639 (the same probe handed to the jobs runner and ingest)
what: `capabilities.build` deliberately re-reads `idle_seconds` on every report, and on a Mac each read is a `/usr/sbin/ioreg -c IOHIDSystem -d 1 -w 0` subprocess. The report runs every 5 s while any lane is syncing and every 60 s otherwise; the jobs runner and ingest ask the same probe on their own cadence.
cost: Estimated 10-30 ms per spawn (fork/exec plus an IOKit dump): ~17,000 spawns a day on a Mac during an all-day upload, ~1,440 idle. Small on its own, but it is a process spawn every 5 s on a laptop on battery, for a number whose resolution the scheduler needs only to the minute (the idle floor is 60-300 s).
evidence: code read; no cache in `MacIdleProbe.seconds_idle` or `default_ioreg_run`. Windows uses `GetLastInputInfo` (no spawn) and is unaffected.
fix: Cache the ioreg answer for ~5 s and extrapolate (`cached + (now - cached_at)`; any input resets it on the next real read). Must keep: None still means "cannot tell, so NOT idle" on both sides; a cached value never claims more idleness than real time allows.

title: Lane B still spends a full-width SSH pool and a recursive NAS listing on every project every pass; CR-381's cheap half was never applied to it
what: Lane B has no SKIP/VERIFY plan and no narrow pool: each project turn spawns rclone lsf (breaker probe, own SSH login) and rclone sync with --sftp-connections 16 --checkers 16, and the + **/Proxy/** filter cannot prune any directory, so every NAS directory of the project (originals included) is listed every pass.
cost: CR-381 measured the same pool flags at 100-180 SSH logins per 27-project pass (1,600-1,950/h) for lane A. Lane B is the same order: ~1,000-1,600 logins/h, 540 rclone spawns/h and 270 recursive SFTP walks/h per idle editor at N=27 (estimated); ~20-30k logins/h at 20 machines x 30 projects.
evidence: Read: lane B always built with self.tuning; for_verify used by lane A only; CR-381 KNOWN_BUGS measurement (lane B was parked on the measured machine).
ledger: related to CR-62 (open: per-project change signal) and CR-381 (lane A only)
fix: (a) When the subpath's previous lane B outcome was NOTHING and nothing failed this pass, build lane B with tuning.for_verify() (4/4); every latch unchanged. (b) Ship the dashboard's per-project tree_sig on the selection reply and SKIP lane B when unchanged since the last clean run, with a max age after which it runs anyway; unknown signature = FULL.

title: CR-381's clean-project skip survives an untick/re-tick and a full <-> upload-only flip, so lane A skips files it has never looked at for up to 2 h
what: A clean check is keyed on subpath only. A flip to upload-only widens lane A's filter to every file (GL-13) but the old video-only 'found nothing' still yields SKIP; a project unticked, written to (notify_change cannot map it while unticked) and re-ticked also SKIPs. Neither _update_known_selection nor _prune_bookkeeping clears _lane_a_clean or _lane_a_changed_at.
cost: Non-video files of a project flipped to upload-only (its documented purpose) do not start uploading for up to lane_a_verify_seconds (7200 s) while the turn record says 'found nothing'; same for a re-ticked project. No loss (removal gate runs its own dry run); CR-383-shaped silent delay in code from 2026-11-05.
evidence: Read: _lane_a_clean is cleared only by _forget_clean_checks (resume, Sync now) and a non-clean run.
fix: Drop clean checks for slugs whose mode changed or that left/entered the selection in _update_known_selection, and prune _lane_a_clean/_lane_a_changed_at in _prune_bookkeeping; or store the filter mode in the clean-check tuple and treat a mismatch as FULL.

title: The skipped-exists alarm and the orphan .partial report hold only the LAST project scanned; tree-wide scans run N times per scan pass
what: refresh_orphan_report runs per project on the 20-turn cadence and all projects are scanned in the same pass; each call replaces the single _orphans / _size_mismatches slot, so the report ends up describing the last project only. The future-dated report was already made per-subpath for exactly this reason; these two were not. scan_trash_dir and _refresh_stray_projects (tree-wide) repeat N times in that pass.
cost: A project with re-exports that copy --ignore-existing will never upload is shown for one project-turn every ~20 passes (~2 h idle) and as 0 the rest of the time, so the SYNC-109 data-loss alarm effectively never stays up. N-1 redundant trash walks (up to 50,000 stats) and marker scans per scan pass.
evidence: Read.
ledger: related to dash-api-5 (dashboard side); companion side new
fix: Key _size_mismatches and _orphans by subpath like _future_dated_by_sub, prune to known rels, report the sum plus the per-subpath list (count stays meaningful for the current dashboard); run scan_trash_dir and _refresh_stray_projects once per pass or on their own interval.

title: Every lane C turn PATCHes the folder config even when it is already running, and reads the full Syncthing config three times per project
what: SYNC-7 removed the no-op unpause PATCH from the between-passes sweep, but the per-turn _set_paused(slug, False) remains unconditional although the turn has just fetched the folder's config (paused included). Each PATCH makes Syncthing save config.xml and broadcast ConfigSaved. The turn also GETs the whole /rest/config three times (repath per project, device ids, verify).
cost: N=27 at ~10 passes/h: ~270 config commits/h and ~810 full-config reads/h per idle editor (estimated); config.xml at 100 folders is ~100-300 KB.
evidence: Read; set_folder_paused is PATCH /rest/config/folders/<id>. Syncthing-side save cost PLAUSIBLE (from its config handler, not measured).
ledger: related to SYNC-7 (fixed for the sweep only)
fix: Return the fetched folder from _reassert_folder_policy and skip the unpause PATCH when paused is False; PATCH as today when the fetch failed. Fetch /rest/config once per turn and share it with repath's per-project check, _remote_device_ids and the verify step.

title: The Syncthing lane polls 3 + 2N REST calls every 15 s for the life of the process, including one expensive /rest/db/status per folder
what: check_once runs ping, connections, full config, then /rest/db/status and /rest/db/completion per expected folder every 15 s, unconditionally, idle or not. Syncthing documents db/status as expensive and provides the events API (FolderSummary, FolderCompletion, StateChanged, FolderErrors) for this.
cost: N=27: 57 requests per 15 s = ~13,700/h, ~330k/day per idle editor, computed by Syncthing beside Resolve; N=100: ~48,000/h (estimated cost per call).
evidence: Read; matches the SYNC-8 docstring's own '3 + 2N requests every 15 s'.
fix: Adaptive cadence: 15 s while syncing/error or after a connection change, back off to 60-120 s after two all-idle polls, reset by a sequencer turn or tray action; or a long-poll /rest/events consumer with a per-folder cache and a reconciliation poll every few minutes. Keep ping at 15 s for the supervisor, the CR-278 heal and the lane C progress token.

title: Breaker and project-dir state files are rewritten every pass when nothing changed; the breaker persists the OLDEST 512 scopes and never prunes unticked ones
what: lane_b_breaker.json is atomically rewritten twice per lane B run and project_dirs.json read and rewritten whole per lane A run regardless of change. _remote_counts (trigger 1's only memory of each scope's NAS size) is never pruned, and its persisted copy is the first 512 keys in insertion order, so once a machine has seen 512 scopes every newer project's count is memory-only and lost on restart.
cost: ~3N small file writes per pass (~810/h at N=27): small. Past 512 lifetime scopes (renames and borrowed subpaths count) a restarted machine cannot trip the 'listed as EMPTY' rule on a newer project's first pass: a commercial-scale cliff.
evidence: Read.
fix: Skip _write_state when the payload equals the last successful one (keep the failure retry); persist the newest 512 scopes or prune to the live selection; write _note_project_dir_seen at most once per project per day and prune entries unseen for 90 days.

title: The 120 s media-tree refresh re-reads every pool clip's proxy state through Resolve, unchanged pool or not
what: _enrich_proxy_keys asks Resolve for Proxy Media Path and Proxy (plus Frames for archive clips) on every pool clip every 120 s with no memory of the previous pass; each 100-clip chunk reconnects, and the uid map (60 s TTL < 120 s refresh) is rebuilt in one lock hold. Without a library the API walk does 5 RPCs per clip in a single _API_LOCK hold.
cost: In-tree measurement 5.5 s per 1,298 clips. Today 5-17 s of Resolve API time per 120 s at idle. At 20,000 clips ~85 s reads + ~2.3 s single-hold uid walk + 200 connects per pass (~80 % of Resolve's scripting capacity); API-fallback machines hold _API_LOCK ~145 s per pass (estimated from 9.4 s / 1,298).
evidence: resolve_bridge.py:1929-1935, :2006-2030, :2139 vs app.py:2102; GOTCHAS section 16; proxy_relink.py:835 only acts on non-working proxies.
fix: Memo uid -> (proxy_path, proxy_state, frames) per project; re-read only new clips, clips whose last state was not working, or after ProjectLibrary.changed(); full re-read every Nth pass; uid-map TTL above the refresh interval. Keep the no-half-enriched-list contract and keep enrichment off _LIBRARY_LOCK.

title: Every bridge call opens a brand-new scriptapp() connection (1/s with the Cards role, every 3 s from the watcher, per enrichment chunk, per relinked clip)
what: connect() calls scriptapp('Resolve') every time with no cached handle: a TCP connect to 1144, a HostApp create/destroy in fuscript, a second connection to Resolve, a TIME_WAIT socket. The Cards engine in the same process holds one steady connection, yet its 1 s sweep reconnects through library_timeline_items -> _timeline_head_locked.
cost: 75 ms per guarded connect and 49 TIME_WAIT sockets measured in LAG-INVESTIGATION.md:138-148/:418. Watcher ~1.3 s/min of lock time connecting; Cards role +~4 s/min; a 1,300-op relink +~85 s; a 20k enrichment pass +200 connects.
evidence: resolve_bridge.py:452 and module docstring lines 7-9; LAG-INVESTIGATION.md:54-55, :145-146; MulticamPipeline cards/resolve_engine.py:265.
fix: Cache the scriptapp object keyed on the fuscript listener pid and Resolve pid script_server already sees; reuse while every probe answers READY with the same pids; drop on non-READY, pid change, any exception, or GetProjectManager() None. Keeps CR-68 and R12 (stale-bridge restart still fires).

title: The watcher stats and realpaths every timeline clip every 3 s, even when the Resolve answer came from the poll cache
what: Every poll reclassifies every item; for canonical-prefix clips not textually under local_root (every clip on a remote editor rig, where P: is the \\localhost\CCSync_P loopback share) that is one exists() and, for present files, one realpath() through the SMB redirector per clip per poll. The per-file realpath is redundant when the cached prefix check passes.
cost: Measured 2,000 files on local NTFS: 57 ms exists + 102 ms realpath = ~160 ms per 3 s poll (~5 % of a core continuously); through loopback SMB estimated 3-10x (0.5-1.6 s per poll). At 20k items it no longer fits the 3 s interval.
evidence: probe classify_probe.py; paths.py:158-163 (_delooped); watcher.py:169-171 memoises the archive/proxy questions but not the classification.
ledger: related to comp-resolve-7 (2026-09-18, FIXED, different question)
fix: Test the cached prefix verdict before the per-file realpath, and memoise path -> OK/MISSING across polls with the _exempt_memo TTL/cap, dropped on the bridge's full walk. Keep BAD_PREFIX detection; never memoise OUT_OF_TREE/FOREIGN offers.

title: A project switch runs one full media-pool walk per pending file move, synchronously on the watcher thread
what: _relink_pending_moves calls relink_moved once per pending entry (30-day window, ledger cap 200), and each call does a complete get_media_pool_items() (library read + full proxy enrichment, or the whole API walk under one lock hold) to look for one old path. K pending moves = K walks of the same pool inside poll_once; a move in a rarely opened project re-costs every switch.
cost: 10 pending moves on a 1,300-clip project: 55-94 s with the watcher not polling and Resolve's scripting saturated; on a 20k-clip pool, tens of minutes per project switch.
evidence: app.py:9445-9456; file_moves.py:953; file_moves.py:1279-1297.
fix: Walk the pool once per _relink_pending_moves call and match all pending entries against it (relink_moved taking pre-walked items); run it on a worker thread, not in the watcher callback. Keep 'only a walk that found the old path retires the entry'.

title: Every relink builds Resolve's full 60-key property dict two to four times plus a fresh connection, while the probed one-arg reader sits unused
what: replace_clip (_file_path_locked/_geometry_locked), link_proxy_media and clip_proxy_state call no-arg GetClipProperty() (12.5 ms) although _clip_property already probes the one-arg overload (0.1 ms) once per process and falls back; _before_mutation adds a forced fresh connect + 3 RPCs per clip.
cost: Per GOTCHAS 16 figures: 1,300-clip FIX ALL / auto proxy relink = 1,300 x (25-50 ms dict + ~65 ms connect) = ~2-2.5 min of extra _API_LOCK time, blocking watcher, b-roll insert and Cards; force refreshes double the geometry reads.
fix: Route those readers through _clip_property (two one-arg reads for geometry); let _before_mutation reuse the cached handle from comp-resolve-2 while keeping the max_age=0 project check. Keep File Path change as the success test.

title: The undo journal rewrites the whole JSON file for every entry (quadratic)
what: record() re-reads, re-parses and re-writes (indent=1, tmp + os.replace) the burst's entire journal per entry, so a burst is O(n^2) in CPU and bytes written.
cost: Measured 1,000 entries 3.7 s, 2,000 entries 13.9 s, final 779 KB, ~780 MB written for one 2,000-clip pass; at the 5,000 cap an estimated ~85 s and ~2 GB. Spent on the relink thread outside _API_LOCK.
evidence: probe journal_probe.py with HOME redirected to scratch.
fix: Keep the open burst in memory and write from it without re-reading, without indent, coalesced (every N entries or 1 s, at burst end, before an undo reads); or JSONL sidecar compacted at burst end. Keep valid JSON after a crash.

title: The CR-68 probe snapshots every process even when nothing listens on 1144, and the disconnection text spawns tasklist every 30 s on top
what: ABSENT is decided from TCP rows alone but every probe also walks a Toolhelp snapshot of all processes; every failed poll's describe_disconnection() spawns tasklist when its 30 s cache lapses, answering a question the snapshot already answered.
cost: Measured 9.2 ms CPU per probe, 8.4 ms of it the snapshot; >= 1 probe per 3 s = ~260 s CPU/day per machine; plus 2 tasklist spawns/min (~209 ms wall, ~19 ms CPU) = 2,880 spawns/day whenever Resolve is closed or unscriptable.
evidence: probe probe.py (tcp 0.27 ms, processes 8.41 ms); tasklist timing.
fix: Return ABSENT from the TCP rows before taking the snapshot (or OpenProcess only the listener/client pids); have _resolve_process_present reuse a Toolhelp snapshot instead of tasklist, keeping its fail-closed bias.

title: The Cards role's refusal watchdog runs PowerShell + WMI every 60 s for as long as a standalone agent is running
what: With cards_agent on and the role refused because a standalone reorder_web.py --agent is running, the watchdog launches powershell Get-CimInstance Win32_Process every minute indefinitely to re-read every command line.
cost: Measured 441-504 ms wall per run, ~114 KB stdout, ~220 ms PowerShell CPU plus WmiPrvSE work; 1,440 launches/day beside Resolve.
evidence: probe cim.py.
ledger: related to RES-7 (2026-09-04, cadence by design)
fix: Toolhelp snapshot first; only when a python/pythonw/node process exists, query CIM for those pids (-Filter ProcessId=...) or read command lines via NtQueryInformationProcess; keep cannot-tell = refuse.

title: plan_relinks re-stats up to four proxy candidates for every clip without a working proxy on every 120 s pass, with no memory
what: find_proxy_on_disk tries 2 extensions x 2 spellings per clip each pass with os.path.exists; the watcher memoises the same question for 60 s and app._media_presence caches originals, but nothing caches the proxies' absence.
cost: Wired rig (local_root on SMB), 5,000-clip pool without Proxy/ files: up to 20,000 failed SMB stats per 120 s (estimated 20-40 s per pass); 80,000 at 20k clips, beyond the interval.
evidence: proxy_relink.py:203-215; app.py:5129.
ledger: related to ops-efficiency-8 / CR-66 (FIXED for originals only)
fix: One listdir per distinct Proxy/ directory per pass with set lookups, or share the watcher's TTL memo; cache absence for at most one pass.

title: Every companion start walks the whole of local_root for *.ccsync-tmp, which on the base rig and wired rigs is the NAS share
what: Startup os.walks every directory under local_root to find interrupted FIX ALL partials and reservations; where local_root is the SMB share that is a full NAS tree enumeration per start, and starts are frequent (supervisor relaunch, OTA, stale-bridge self-restart after each Resolve quit).
cost: 50,000 files locally 0.12-0.35 s (measured); over SMB estimated 40-200 s of NAS metadata load per start at 100 projects, more at 500.
evidence: fixer.py:795; app.py:10581-10587; app.py:4966 (restart on Resolve exit).
fix: fix_clip records each tmp/reservation it creates in a small state file; sweep only those, falling back to the full walk when the file is absent or local_root is a local disk.

title: Every card lookup that finds a copy the ledger mirror now has rewrites and fsyncs the whole local-copies file, once per file
where: companion/src/ccsync_companion/field_mode.py:737-751 (LedgerView._raw -> local.forget), field_mode.py:684-696 (LocalCopies.forget -> _atomic_write + fsync); via card_verdict (field_service.py:479) and field_copy.py:538 verified_record
what: _raw is a per-file lookup and calls forget() on that file's covered rows; forget() rewrites field-local-copies.jsonl in full with tmp+fsync+replace. The one-time catch-up becomes N rewrites of M rows: O(N x M) bytes and N fsyncs.
cost: First /field/api/state after each ledger sync following a card copy, and every re-run of a card already at a destination. Measured 7.48 s for a 1,000-file card copied to two drives (2,000 rows); at the 60,000-row cap ~6 MB per rewrite, ~6 GB and 1,000 fsyncs for a 1,000-file card (estimated tens of seconds to minutes). The page shows 'Companion not answering' meanwhile.
evidence: probe_forget.py: 7.48 s, all in forget(); code read of _raw/forget/_atomic_write.
fix: Collect covered rows during a verdict / verify loop and flush with one forget() at the end (or lazily). Keep: a covered row is never counted twice (_raw already de-duplicates via seen) and is eventually dropped from disk.

title: A card verdict opens a fresh SQLite connection, re-runs the schema, and linearly scans every local copy, once per file on the card, every 20 s
where: companion/src/ccsync_companion/field_mode.py:336 (card_verdict per-file copies_of), field_mode.py:672-682 (LocalCopies.matching full scan); ledger_mirror.py:337-350 + 172-181 (where -> _connect: mkdir, connect, PRAGMA WAL, executescript(SCHEMA)); field_service.py:43 VERDICT_TTL_SECONDS=20, field.js polls state every 4 s (1 s while copying)
what: Per-file lookups each pay connection setup plus schema DDL plus an O(M) Python scan of up to 60,000 local rows; nothing is shared across the files of one verdict.
cost: Per inserted card every 20 s while the field page is open, and after every copy. Measured 0.90 s per verdict at 1,000 files / 4,000 local rows (~4.5% of a core per card); 9.81 s at 2,000 files / 60,000 rows (~50% of a core per card, 10 s state requests), on a field laptop that is also copying.
evidence: probe_verdict.py: mirror.where 1.00-1.34 ms per call, matching 0.154 ms at 4k rows and 3.47 ms at 60k rows, card_verdict 0.90 s and 9.81 s.
fix: One mirror connection per verdict (where_many or a held connection) and SCHEMA once per process; index LocalCopies rows by (name.lower(), size) maintained by add/forget. Keep _present and the mtime slack per row.

title: A dialog that raises on a tray click thread leaves its Tcl interpreter pinned for the life of the process
where: companion/src/ccsync_companion/ui_dispatch.py:544-553 (dispatch inline path try/finally reclaim_mine); ui_dispatch.py:146-158 (_Job.run, macOS)
what: When fn raises, reclaim_mine runs while the traceback still holds fn's frame locals (widgets, root), so _try_free sees refs above baseline and keeps the pin. On Windows the building thread is a per-click _spawn thread or the per-open work-window thread and exits next, so the interpreter can never be freed.
cost: ~1.8 MB per failed dialog build, permanent; triggers are TclErrors from RDP reconnects or display changes mid-build. Rare: a few MB a month on a machine RDP'd into daily, plus a WARNING with holder chains each time.
evidence: probe_pin.py with a fake root/tkapp: return path leaves 0 pinned after the thread exits, raise path leaves 1 pinned on a dead thread with the module's own 'still referenced (5 refs, baseline 4)' warning.
fix: Catch BaseException, traceback.clear_frames(exc.__traceback__), then reclaim_mine, then re-raise, in dispatch() and _Job.run. Pin-at-birth and free-on-building-thread rules are untouched.

title: The menu fingerprint carries lane C's live byte and file counts, so the menu is rebuilt every tick while lane C uploads
where: companion/src/ccsync_companion/tray.py:3942-3945 (_menu_fingerprint includes raw s.detail); sync/syncthing_lane.py:921-929 (detail embeds counts and sizes); tray.py:5252-5255; tray_native.py:1883-1889 -> _build_nsmenu on macOS
what: The fingerprint is deliberately coarse everywhere else but includes each lane's raw detail, which for lane C embeds moving counts, so every changed count is a full _build_menu and on macOS a full NSMenu rebuild with new ObjC targets on the Tk-Aqua main thread.
cost: Up to 43,200 rebuilds a day during lane C uploads instead of on state changes (probe: 300 distinct fingerprints in 300 ticks). Windows: nil (~6 us build, free assignment). macOS: estimated 1-3 ms of main-thread work per rebuild.
evidence: probe_snapshot.py fingerprint churn; code read of the fingerprint and the darwin __setattr__ hook.
fix: Fingerprint a digit-normalised detail (replace each run of digits with '#'); the live numbers stay on the tooltip, as the fingerprint's own docstring intends.

title: The 2 s tray tick re-reads and re-parses site.json three times, and the pulse thread wakes 2.7 times a second with nothing to pulse
where: companion/src/ccsync_companion/tray.py:2962, 2971-2975 (cached_site via _dashboard_url and three feature_enabled calls), tray.py:3002/2531 (second app.lane_statuses() per tick), tray.py:5276-5309 (pulse loop sleeps 0.375 s forever)
what: site._brand_site already memoises the manifest by mtime for exactly this caller, but cached_site/feature_enabled (what the tray calls) re-read and re-parse the file every time. The pulse thread polls a tuple every 375 ms even when nothing pulses.
cost: Per machine per day: 216,000 small file opens (130,000 site.json parses) through on-access scanning, plus ~230,000 pulse-thread wakeups. Measured snapshot total 0.33 ms per tick (~15 CPU-s a day), so the saving is wakeups and disk I/O beside Resolve.
evidence: probe_snapshot.py: 5 read_text per snapshot (site.json x3, eula_accepted.json, ytdl-attestation.json), 0.317 ms per snapshot.
ledger: related to comp-app-4; new for the site.json half
fix: Route feature_enabled() with no site argument through _brand_site() (still fail-closed); pass the snapshot's statuses into _current_project_line; let the pulse loop wait on an Event set when pulsing starts.

title: Ingest asks tasklist before every extracted frame: the Resolve probe costs 2.7x the frames it guards
what: _should_stop() re-runs the full gate before every stage and before every one-frame seek in _make_frames. In the default idle run mode with the editor away, the gate reaches _resolve_running() = resolve_prefs.resolve_is_running(), an uncached tasklist spawn (proxy_gen caches the same probe for 60 s). broll_ingest_skip_while_resolve defaults to True; music inherits the same path.
cost: ~29 tasklist spawns per 90 s clip (frames every <=4 s plus stage checks). Measured: 23 tasklist calls 5.4 s vs the 23 frame seeks 1.96 s. 400 clips of 60 s ~8,000 spawns (~30 min wall); 2,000-clip batch ~40,000 spawns (1.8-2.6 h).
evidence: Code read; tasklist timed at 0.16 s (10 calls) and 0.235 s (23 calls under load); frames_probe.py on a synthetic 90 s 1080p h264 clip.
ledger: new (MED-9 2026-08-11 fixed the same pattern in proxy_gen only)
fix: TTL-cache (5-15 s) the Resolve probe for the between-stage/between-frame _should_stop, keep the fresh probe for the tick gate, keep fail-closed. Secondary: one select= ffmpeg pass beat 23 seeks (0.64 s vs 1.96 s) on a 90 s clip; use only below a duration threshold.

title: The ingest state file is re-serialised whole, pretty-printed, at every stage of every item: O(n^2) bytes per batch
what: Every checkpoint deep-copies and rewrites the whole batch plus every retained staging drop (7-day retention) with the pure-Python indent=2 encoder under the GIL. One item passes ~12 saves, so bytes written grow as ~12 n x size(n).
cost: Measured per save: 400 items 15.7 ms / 1.35 MB; 2,000 items 84 ms / 6.75 MB. 400-clip card ~4,800 saves = ~6.5 GB written, ~75 s CPU; 2,000-clip card (server MAX_BATCH_ITEMS) ~24,000 saves = ~160 GB written, ~34 min CPU (totals estimated from measured per-save cost).
evidence: save_probe.py: synthetic snapshot shaped like _save's; compact separators 6.2-6.8x faster and 31% smaller.
ledger: new (comp-broll-music-1 2026-09-03 fixed thread safety, not cost)
fix: (a) separators=(',', ':'); (b) dirty flag flushed at most every 2-5 s from the tick, synchronous only at transitions a restart cannot rediscover (claim, lease change, held-for-base-rig, batch end). Crunch steps re-derive done-ness from artifacts on disk, so a lost checkpoint costs a re-run stage, never a wrong one. Keep per-thread tmp + _save_lock.

title: The music page's 30 s Resolve-status poll re-launches the onefile companion exe every time, even with Resolve closed and the tab hidden
what: Each /music/status is subprocess.run of the frozen companion re-entered with --music-resolve-worker: onefile extraction to %TEMP%, interpreter boot, a fresh fuscript connection, deletion. The 3 s probe cache cannot coalesce a 30 s cadence, the page does not check document.hidden, and the parent never checks whether Resolve's script server is up before spawning. /status, b-roll Send to Resolve and music send pay one extraction per click too.
cost: 120 spawns/hour per open music tab; at PRAC-77's measured 116 MB per extraction ~14 GB/hour of %TEMP% writes and ~120 interpreter boots and fuscript connects per hour (estimated), per editor.
evidence: Code read; import ccsync_companion.app measured at 0.16 s, so the cost is the extraction, not Python imports.
ledger: related to PRAC-77 (open) and comp-broll-music-3 (fixed the burst, not the cadence)
fix: Parent answers without a child when script_server.state() is not ready (TCP table, CR-68-safe); page skips ticks while document.hidden and backs off to 60-120 s. Keep the killable child for real Resolve calls (MED-3). Onedir (PRAC-77) removes the per-call extraction.

title: Ingest uploads spawn two rclone processes (copyto + lsjson verify) per artifact, five artifacts per clip, one at a time
what: Each artifact (poster, sprite, preview proxy, edit proxy, original) is its own rclone copyto and SFTP session, followed by an rclone lsjson session to compare size. rclone already fails a size mismatch after transfer and the server stats every file before marking it live, so lsjson is a third size check.
cost: 10 rclone spawns + 10 SSH handshakes per clip, serial: 4,000 for 400 clips, 20,000 for 2,000. At an estimated 0.5-1 s each, ~0.5-1 h or ~3-5.5 h of overhead before bytes move; three of five files per clip are sub-MB stills where the handshake is the whole cost.
evidence: Code read; per-spawn NAS cost not measured (NAS off limits).
fix: Drop the lsjson verify (rclone's own size check plus the server stat remain); send poster + sprite in one rclone copy --files-from staged under their server-allocated layout. Keep original-first ordering, copyto for server-chosen names, far-side .partial.

title: Startup walks the whole tree twice for two leftover-file sweeps that were meant to share one walk
what: sweep_stale_partials re-walks local_root with the same pruning right after fixer.walk_ccsync_tmp_files, which COMP-GUARD-1 split out so the startup sweeps share one walk. Not gated on mode, so the base rig walks P: over SMB twice.
cost: Once per start (several per day: PRAC-77 counted 24 of 55 starts as restarts on Resolve exit). 0.1 s per 50k-file local walk measured; tens of seconds of NAS metadata traffic per extra walk on the base rig (estimated).
evidence: Code read; walk_probe.py.
fix: Collect Proxy/*.partial in walk_ccsync_tmp_files' loop and pass the list to sweep_stale_partials, as tmp_files is passed to the reservation sweep.

title: llama-server's log is appended for the life of the install
what: Every server start opens ~/.ccsync/state/broll_vlm_server.log in append mode; the server restarts after every gate close (editor back), and nothing truncates or rotates the file.
cost: Estimated ~20-50 KB per start plus ~1-2 KB per described clip; a few MB per thousand clips, never reclaimed.
evidence: Code read.
fix: In start_server, rotate to one .1 generation when the log exceeds ~5 MB before opening it.

title: The peaks recipe holds the whole decoded audio in RAM, then makes five more copies of it
what: _read_pcm keeps every PCM block in a list, joins them (2x), and peaks_bytes does astype(int32) and np.abs (4x each) before reducing to one byte per 40 samples; peak transient is about 6x the PCM size inside the companion.
cost: 57.6 MB PCM per audio hour. Measured transient: +288 MB for a 1 h clip, +864 MB for a 3 h interview (about 1.04 GB resident with the chunk list), once per peaks job, beside Resolve on the base rig or an editor machine.
evidence: peaks.py probe under tracemalloc: 1.0h +288 MB, 3.0h +864 MB; streaming binner byte-identical with about 10 MB extra.
ledger: new (comp-ytdl-jobs-4 / CR-237 fixed the drain's truncation, not its size)
fix: Bin in the drain thread block by block (carry remainder to a multiple of 80 bytes); identical bytes, so the library_engine pin holds; keep the pcm_thread.is_alive() truncation check and failure hand-back.

title: Every job-runner tick spawns tasklist 1-4 times, even when nothing can be claimed
what: runnable_kinds() goes through capabilities.build, whose cached path still calls resolve_running_fn (a tasklist spawn) every time; the gate probes Resolve again and a claim twice more, although the hardware answer runnable_kinds needs is cached.
cost: Measured 1 spawn per tick with the editor present, 2 when idle, 4 with an offer (+1 per media job); ticks every 20 s with a non-empty queue, 80 s empty: 45-360 tasklist spawns/hour/machine at about 0.16 s wall each, for weeks, beside Resolve; about 7,000/hour across 20 machines.
evidence: count.py with the real JobRunner.tick(): 1/2/4 Resolve probes per tick in the three states; tl.py: tasklist median 0.164 s.
fix: Read capabilities once per tick and pass it through; answer runnable_kinds from cached hardware fields only; give resolve_process_state a shared 5-10 s TTL, fail-closed on None kept.

title: A stale offer plus an unreachable dashboard: a claim attempt and a full traceback every 20 s, and the gate says ready
what: default_request raises on a transport failure; _claim does not catch it (the heartbeat does), so the tick raises, _offered is never cleared and state stays ready; only a successful report reply replaces the offer.
cost: A laptop off the tailnet holding an offer: every 20 s one claim attempt (up to 20 s blocked), 1-4 tasklist spawns and a traceback, 180/hour (about 5-10 MB of log a day, evicting useful history through rotation), while Settings and the report say ready for fleet work.
evidence: stale.py: 10 ticks -> 10 claim attempts, offered still [5], state ready, wait 20.0, 10 tracebacks.
fix: Catch transport failures in _claim: one INFO line, clear _offered, return None so the tick lands in nothing_offered and backs off; leave the 401/403 handling (wire-5) as it is.

title: Two machines can write the same .partial in the shared vault after a lease expiry, and the loser deletes the winner's file
what: Rule 2 is enforced per process (claim_partial is an in-process set) but the output is in the shared vault; the heartbeat keeps working through transport failures, so a dashboard outage longer than the 300 s lease lets another machine claim the same job and write the same <final>.partial.
cost: Dashboard down more than 300 s while a long proxy encodes: B truncates A's .partial with -y; A gets 410, kills and discard()s the file B is writing; B's os.replace fails after minutes of encode on two machines, or a mixed file is published.
evidence: Code reading of the three sites and the lease contract in docs/API.md 6c; not reproduced.
fix: Per-job partial name (<final>.<job id>.partial): still matched by every *.partial lane filter, and discard can only remove its own bytes; _publish's re-check still decides the winner.

title: Media recipes spawn one more ffprobe than they need
what: proxy-480p runs probe_video and probe_audio as two ffprobe processes over the same source; peaks probes before every decode for a duration used only for the realtime figure and the no-audio verdict on failure.
cost: One extra ffprobe per proxy and per peaks job (estimated 0.1-0.3 s each, more over SMB, 120 s timeout on a wedged share), hundreds per episode.
evidence: Code reading; not timed.
fix: One combined ffprobe for the proxy; for peaks probe only after a non-zero exit and derive the duration from len(raw)/16000. No argv the page reads changes.

title: A card folder that cannot be read vanishes from the listing, and the card is then 'Safe to format'
what: list_card swallows OSError from scandir of a folder and from an entry stat, so an unreadable folder's files are absent from `files`; the field verdict judges only what was listed and nothing marks the listing partial.
cost: Flaky card: DCIM/101MEDIA throws EIO, 100MEDIA files are at home -> 'Safe to format: all 3 files are at home'; 101MEDIA footage has no copy and is formatted away. The copy run copies the same short list, so lanes are green too.
evidence: probe_unreadable.py: scandir raises for 101MEDIA -> 3 of 6 files listed -> verdict safe, safeToFormat=True.
fix: list_card returns an `unreadable` list like LedgerScan; card_verdict refuses safeToFormat (state 'incomplete', naming the folder) while it is non-empty; copy run reports it.

title: 'Safe to format' ignores originals whose extension is not on an allow-list (Nikon N-RAW .NEV and others)
what: is_judged is an allow-list (MASTER/AUDIO/MEDIA exts + extras); .NEV, .ARX, .cine, .CRW, .ERF, .RWL, .M2T, .MOD, .VOB are not judged (fail-open) and FieldCopier._record drops them.
cost: Nikon card with N-RAW video + stills: 'Safe to format' once the stills have two copies, whatever happened to the .NEV clips; an N-RAW-only card reads 'Nothing on this card needs backing up'.
evidence: Inline probe: is_judged False for .NEV/.ARX/.cine/.CRW/.ERF/.M2T/.MOD/.VOB/.RWL; card_verdict of one 5 GB .NEV -> state empty, 'Nothing on this card needs backing up'.
fix: Judge every file except a deny-list (sidecars, thumbnails, proxies, system/temp, ._ twins); add the missing exts to the ledger rules separately.

title: The verdict rewrites field-local-copies.jsonl with fsync once per file after a sync: 28 s for a 2,000-file card
what: LedgerView._raw calls LocalCopies.forget per lookup that the mirror now covers; forget rewrites the whole jsonl + fsync. One rewrite per file, inside the page's state request; overlapping 4 s polls start more verdicts. add() is quadratic too.
cost: First verdict per card after each delivering sync: 500 files 10.6 s, 2,000 files 28.0 s page stall + fsync storm; at the 60k-row cap ~18 MB per rewrite, ~36 GB written for a 2,000-file card (estimated).
evidence: probe_verdict.py: F=500 cover -> 10.60 s; F=2000 cover -> 28.01 s; local rows 4000 -> 0.
fix: Collect covered rows and forget once per verdict (or reconcile on the sync thread after a pull); index LocalCopies by (name_lc,size) and (volume_id,path).

title: Every verdict reopens SQLite per file, re-reads field-state.json six times per file and scans all local copies per file: 4.4 s per 2,000-file card every 20 s
what: Per judged file: one SQLite connect + PRAGMA + executescript(SCHEMA), ~6 FieldStore file reads+parses via KindResolver, a linear LocalCopies scan; at home each NAS copy is stat'ed over SMB. Lane planning repeats the per-file lookups.
cost: Page polls 4 s idle / 1 s copying, verdict TTL 20 s and invalidated by lane ends/syncs. 2,000 files: 4.4 s (1.8 s SQLite, 1.1 s LocalCopies scan, 0.67 s for 12,000 state-file reads); +~6 s at 20k local rows (estimated); +2-6 s SMB stats at home (estimated).
evidence: probe_verdict.py F=2000: 4.42 s, field-state.json reads=12000, sqlite connects=2000; cProfile breakdown.
fix: One connection (or one json_each batch query) per verdict, schema once per process, kinds/guesses/info snapshotted per verdict, indexed LocalCopies, pool presence cached per verdict.

title: Cards in fixed readers (CFexpress B) are reported to the sorter but cannot be copied by the companion or the field page
what: 7ac37ed made sorter_cards report fixed-disk cards; card_copy._find_card/_card_gone, field_service._cards_from and field_copy._card_present still look only at removable volumes.
cost: Every sorter card-ingest of a CFexpress B / BMCC SSD card fails non-retryably ('not in a card reader on this computer'); the field page cannot back it up and offers it as a destination (kind unknown).
evidence: Code read; git show --stat 7ac37ed touched sorter_cards only.
fix: One shared 'is this volume a card' predicate (removable, or fixed with a camera layout) used by card_copy, field_service and field_copy; exclude such volumes from destinations.

title: The ledger outbox is quadratic to flush and fully re-parsed on every field-page poll
what: Each 500-copy batch re-reads the file twice, re-serialises every line with sort_keys and rewrites + fsyncs it; pending() parses the whole file per page poll and per flusher tick (no backoff on transport errors).
cost: Measured flush (network excluded): 10k 1.0 s, 40k 20.9 s, 80k 73.6 s; 200k cap ~7-8 min and ~11 GB written (extrapolated). pending() 0.26 s at 80k on every 1 s poll during a copy.
evidence: probe_outbox.py at 10k/40k/80k.
fix: Send from one read with a sent-offset, drop delivered lines in one rewrite at the end (or a SQLite outbox), cache pending() by size+mtime; keep 'nothing deleted before a 200' and the rejected file.

title: The mirror is keyed on the volumes plugged in now: every card in or out re-pulls everything (NAS included) and deletes away drives' copies
what: sync() pulls for the current attachment set (cards included); a different set resets the cursor to '' and _forget_other_volumes deletes rows of unplugged drives; _root_by_vid keeps an unplugged drive's letter so _present drops its copies. Both contradict 'a copy on a drive that is away is believed'.
cost: Each card insert re-downloads all rows incl. nas:... (estimated 10^5-10^6 rows, 20-200 pages over Tailscale, tens-hundreds of MB). Card copied to D1 and D2, D1 bagged, next card in, sync -> first card falls to one copy and is re-copied.
evidence: Code read: `same = meta volumes == want`, else cursor '' and _forget_other_volumes(ids).
fix: Pull for a persistent growing set (volumes ever recorded + pool), cursor per volume, never forget on unplug; drop stale _root_by_vid entries each scan.

title: Physical-disk key cached by drive letter for the process lifetime: two partitions of one disk can count as two copies
what: _lane_key caches physical_key(root) by root path forever; letters and device numbers are reassigned while the companion runs for weeks, and the stale key is persisted into LocalCopies rows' phys.
cost: E: was disk:3; today a two-partition SSD (disk:2) is E: and F:, both 'ours' -> keys disk:3 and disk:2 -> two counted copies on one physical disk -> 'Safe to format'. Also parallel lanes onto one disk.
evidence: Code read against file_verdict's promise that two partitions of one disk never make two.
ledger: new (regression of the 2026-11-10 review's physical-disk rule)
fix: Re-ask the IOCTL per scan or key the cache by serial+letter and drop absent volumes.

title: A removable volume holding footage is re-listed in full and re-posted every 10 s whenever its free space moves
what: The relist signature includes free bytes; a volume being written to is re-walked each tick (reading every .xml head and .wav header) and its whole listing POSTed. A removable field drive with a recorder/BMCC backup (media at depth 2) is a 'generic' card.
cost: 20k files: 0.8-1.2 s per list on NVMe (slower on USB HDD, competing with the copy), 6 re-lists/min, 1.8 MB body each; idle every 300 s. Field page re-lists at its 4 s poll.
evidence: probe_listcard.py: list_card 0.80 s, 20005 files, 2000 xml reads, 1.8 MB body; one minute of ticks while written -> 6 full re-lists, 5.1 s.
fix: Leave free out of the relist signature (root+capacity+root mtime), skip running copies' destinations, gzip the cards POST.

title: The Python copier's 'read back in full' verify reads the OS page cache, not the media
what: verify_whole re-reads the partial right after writing it with a plain buffered open; the pages are still cached, so the hash checks memory, not what reached the drive.
cost: Every Python-copier copy (Macs, PCs without TeraCopy) is recorded verified 'full' without proving the medium; a corrupting USB bridge yields copies that count toward 'safe to format'.
evidence: Code read; no FILE_FLAG_NO_BUFFERING / F_NOCACHE / fadvise in the module.
fix: Verify with an uncached read (Windows FILE_FLAG_NO_BUFFERING, macOS F_NOCACHE, Linux fadvise DONTNEED after fsync); keep the hash-while-copying pass.

title: TeraCopy's wait spawns tasklist every 5 s per lane for the whole copy
what: wait_for_job calls _is_running (a tasklist subprocess) on every poll even while the history DB says the job is running.
cost: 186 ms per tasklist measured; 3 lanes x 1 h = 2,160 spawns, ~6.7 min of process time beside the copy.
evidence: Measure-Command over 5 tasklist runs: 186 ms each.
fix: Check the process only when the record is missing/locked or copied without verify; or enumerate processes via ctypes.

title: Every lane reads the whole card on its own; three destinations read the card three times at once
what: One CardJob per lane group, all concurrent, each reading every source file; on the Python path a single read + hash could fan out to N writers.
cost: 256 GB card to 3 drives = 768 GB read in three interleaved streams from one reader (estimated 1.5-3x slower when the reader is the bottleneck). TeraCopy path cannot share a read.
evidence: Code read; estimated.
fix: Fan-out copy for the Python copier (one read/hash, N partial writers, each verified); a failed writer drops out without stopping the read.

title: Proxy-by-name rule has drifted from the ledger's, and the field page never uses the server's rules
what: field_mode uses `S03\.mp4$` and the built-in Rules copy; the ledger uses `\dS\d{2}\.mp4$` and its own rules_doc, so the two disagree and server-side rule changes never reach the page.
cost: C0001S01.MP4 is a proxy to the ledger, a master to the page (extra 'short' files, safe direction); future server-side exts missed by the page.
evidence: Code read of both regexes.
fix: Cache the server's rules_doc with the mirror pull and build field_mode's Rules from it, one shared proxy regex.

title: Every machine's unchanged manifest and media tree are deleted and rewritten in full every 10 minutes
what: The companion force-resends local_manifest and media_tree every 600 s even when unchanged, and the dashboard answers each resend with DELETE + re-INSERT of up to 4,000 editor_media and 4,000 media_tree_clips rows per ticked project. The rewrite also bumps editor_media_project.reported_at, which invalidates the owed-files cache fingerprint.
cost: Measured per ticked project, unchanged: 27.5 ms + 0.84 MB WAL (manifest) and 30.6 ms + 0.80 MB WAL (media tree). Today ~40 project-ticks: ~9.5 GB/day written for no change. At 20 machines x 10 ticks: 0.55 MB/s, ~47 GB/day, ~11.6 s write-lock time per 10 min; both tables (156 + 147 MB) rewritten several times an hour, pinned by hourly snapshots (estimated).
evidence: Probe on a 20-machine fill of the real schema (populate.py / probe.py in the scratch folder); the report handler has no digest or compare before calling replace.
fix: Store a per-project digest on editor_media_project (and for the media tree); skip the replace when unchanged and touch only the small row; prune big-table rows via the small row by PK prefix; fingerprint the owed cache on the digest. Keep the 600 s resend.

title: Overlapping long backlog reads can starve WAL checkpoints, and the WAL file never shrinks
where: dashboard/src/ccsync_dashboard/db.py:710-728 (connect: no journal_size_limit or checkpoint policy); readers db.py:11845 via ui_home.py:423 and ui.py:1870
what: The WAL restarts only when no reader holds a snapshot using it. The admin backlog read takes ~0.9 s at 20 machines here (6 s at 50 editors per PL-RES-74) and is polled every 2 s per tab; continuous overlap makes every commit append. No journal_size_limit, so the -wal file keeps its high-water size.
cost: Probe: one replace every 50 ms with 2 overlapping readers grew the WAL to 549 MB in 45 s (0 readers: 5 MB). At today's cadence and query speed it stayed 6-8 MB, so it needs 20+ machines on NAS CPU or 3+ admin tabs; then ~2 GB/hour of /data at the dash-db-1 write rate, never returned.
evidence: walstarve.py and walstarve_real.py in the scratch folder.
fix: PRAGMA journal_size_limit (e.g. 64 MB) in connect; collector runs wal_checkpoint(RESTART) with a bounded wait each prune cycle and logs an oversized WAL. Shortening the reads (PL-RES-74) removes the overlap.

title: editor_media and media_tree_clips store a long TEXT composite key twice (rowid table + autoindex)
what: Rowid tables with a composite TEXT PRIMARY KEY keep the row and a full copy of the key in sqlite_autoindex; every lookup and replace touches both b-trees.
cost: At 20 machines x 10 ticks: editor_media 156.2 -> 100.8 MB WITHOUT ROWID (-35%), one project replace 15.7 -> 12.6 ms (-20%); media_tree_clips 146.6 -> 120.7 MB (-18%), 19.8 -> 17.3 ms. nas_media is not a candidate (178 -> 217 MB).
evidence: norowid.py in the scratch folder.
fix: One migration step rebuilding both tables WITHOUT ROWID; since both are full-replace caches repopulated within 10 minutes, the step can recreate them empty, keeping boot cost near zero.

title: The hourly prune full-scans the largest tables while holding the write lock
what: EXPLAIN shows SCAN for editor_media/media_tree_clips/missing_files/editor_media_project by refreshed_at, lane_report_history (no index), transfer_history by received_at (indexed on completed_at), completion_history twice with a temp b-tree, and nas_media NOT IN (800k rows), all in one transaction committed afterwards.
cost: Hourly; 352 ms steady state at the 20-machine fill on NVMe (1-2 s on NAS estimated), blocking every writer meanwhile; linear in machines x ticks.
evidence: Query plans and timing from probe.py.
fix: Delete media rows by PK prefix for stale editor_media_project pairs; purge nas_media only for inactive project ids; prune transfer_history on an indexed column; commit between groups. Do not index editor_media.refreshed_at.

title: lane_report_history and completion_history are written and pruned but nothing displays them
what: No route, template or alert reads either table; the only readers are the person-data export/purge, the machine rename and upsert_completion reading its own last row.
cost: ~200 extra SELECTs/min at 20 machines x 10 ticks in the collector, the hourly thinning GROUP BY over ~170k rows, ~72k lane rows/month, plus schema/export/prune surface.
evidence: grep of both table names across dashboard/src.
fix: Give them a reader (per-lane state timeline) or stop writing and drop them in a migration, updating the export table list.

title: The home page computes the fleet backlog three times per render, and each pair's download diff twice
what: One admin GET / runs fetch_sync_backlog three times (600 originals queries for 200 pairs, 9 connections, 2,793 statements); within it the proxy NOT EXISTS anti-join runs once for totals and again for the 50 names.
cost: 20-machine fill on this desktop: GET / 2.8 s; /partials/home-transfers 0.91 s and /partials/transfers 1.0 s, each polled every 2 s; 99% of fetch_sync_backlog time is SQL. Today ~170 ms per call.
evidence: trace_pages.py and profile_backlog.py in the scratch folder.
fix: As part of PL-RES-74: compute once per request and pass it down; fetch totals and first 50 names in one pass with window aggregates.

title: The selection reply re-sends the fleet-wide project_roots map every 30 s, and its per-response timestamp defeats the companion's write-on-change cache
what: GET /api/v1/selection/<editor>?machine= answers with every sticky Resolve-project mapping in the fleet (project_roots grows with every mapping and is pruned only by an admin delete) plus generated_at stamped to the second. The companion fetches every 30 s and its AUDIT_2 P11 write-on-change guard compares the whole response including the timestamp, so every fetch is a full download and a tmp+replace rewrite of selection.json.
cost: 2,880 fetches/day per machine. 100 mappings: 23 KB per reply (measured) = 66 MB/day down and 66 MB/day of editor SSD writes per machine. 500 projects: 104 KB = 300 MB/day per machine, 6 GB/day across 20 machines, for an answer that changes a few times a week.
evidence: probe_views.py: _selection_view 23,054 B (project_roots 18,770 B) at 100 projects, 103,791 B (95,170 B) at 500; selection.py:350-390 compares response == self._last_written on the parsed dict that always carries a new generated_at.
fix: Companion: compare the response with generated_at removed. Dashboard: strong ETag over the response minus generated_at, 304 on If-None-Match; a 304 counts as a successful live fetch (comp-sync-14 stamp), never as unreachable (AUDIT_2 CORE-H9), and the editor-keyed cache rule (bug-comp-syncthing-6) is unchanged.

title: The report holds the database write lock across a filesystem walk of the Projects tree (CR-379 rival check)
where: dashboard/src/ccsync_dashboard/api.py:10981 (holds.begin = BEGIN IMMEDIATE), api.py:11122 (_auto_map_has_rival), api.py:4327-4357 (provision.scan_unregistered_dirs, 60 s cache)
what: The auto-map block runs after BEGIN IMMEDIATE and before the first commit at 11376. On a cache miss _auto_map_has_rival os.walks projects_dir (depth up to 8, pruned at markers) with the write lock held. When a rival is found the mapping is not written, so the walk repeats after every 60 s cache expiry for as long as that Resolve project stays open.
cost: Measured 46-51 ms for a warm synthetic 500-project tree on local SSD; on the NAS with a cold ARC or during a scrub estimated hundreds of ms to seconds, during which the collector, session touches and every other machine's report wait on the 5 s busy_timeout (the 2026-09-03 database-is-locked shape). Ordering confirmed; NAS cost estimated.
evidence: Read of api_report statement order; _WriteHolds.begin executes BEGIN IMMEDIATE (api.py:133-139); timed scan_unregistered_dirs; api.py:10973-10976 already states no write transaction may be open across a lookup (LG-4).
ledger: new; related to CR-379 (fixed) and CR-351
fix: Compute detected_slug, the confident match and the rival verdict before holds.begin (reads plus a walk), keep only db.sticky_project_root inside the transaction. Keep the rival refusal, the 60 s cache and 'tree unreadable means ask'.

title: standins_known re-sends up to 200 archive paths on every report reply to every machine
where: dashboard/src/ccsync_dashboard/api.py:11777; dashboard/src/ccsync_dashboard/db.py:11348 (GROUP BY over all of broll_standins with a sort, per report)
what: The reply always carries the full fleet stand-in list whether or not it changed since the last reply to that machine.
cost: Reply 292 B -> 14,181 B with 200 stand-ins (measured). Per machine 20 MB/day at the 60 s cadence, 242 MB/day at the 5 s active cadence, plus a companion JSON parse per tick. Live stand-in count not read (rule), so daily figures scale linearly from 200.
evidence: probe_report2.py with 200 seeded broll_standins rows.
ledger: related to wire-3 (bug-hunt-2026-09-18b, correctness of the same list)
fix: Add standins_known.sig; the companion echoes the last sig it applied; send rels only when the sigs differ. Absent stays 'does not know', empty stays 'none'; an old companion never echoes a sig and keeps getting the full list.

title: Two to three SQLite opens per companion request where one is needed
where: dashboard/src/ccsync_dashboard/api.py:10918 (read_identity_token_ex without conn=), also 2991, 3056, 5607, 11957, 12452; api.py:2623/2629 (identity_bar opens two per mounted fleet API call); api.py:11720 (music_cancel_requested opens music.db on every report)
what: auth._identity_revoked opens its own db.connect (4 PRAGMAs incl. journal_mode=WAL) whenever no connection is passed, although each route already holds one from get_conn; the music cancel lookup opens music.db read-only on every report even with no ingest batch anywhere.
cost: Measured 3 sqlite3.connect per report vs 1 needed, 0.155 ms each locally (more on ZFS with the -shm mapping); at 20 machines x 5 s, about 8 needless opens/s plus one per fleet-job and ingest heartbeat.
evidence: probe_report2.py call-site counter: 200 x _identity_revoked, 200 x music_cancel_requested for 200 reports.
fix: Pass conn=conn at the six call sites; one connection shared by both halves of identity_bar; gate the music/b-roll cancel lookups on an in-process 'a cancel may be pending' flag or short TTL (the heartbeat 410 stays authoritative). Revocation still fails open on a read error.

title: Each light report writes about 28 KB of WAL, much of it re-stamping unchanged state
where: dashboard/src/ccsync_dashboard/api.py:10984-11015 (clear_report_refused, record_known_editor, record_report_auth, touch_editor_report_token), api.py:11169-11218 (store_* unconditional SET ...=NULL updates), api.py:11352 (replace_active_transfers)
what: A report with nothing new still runs 12 UPDATE, 8 INSERT and 5 DELETE statements; UPDATEs without an IS NOT guard rewrite their page even when values are identical.
cost: Measured 275 WAL frames for 40 reports (~7 pages, 28 KB per report). 4 machines: 160 MB/day idle, 1.9 GB/day syncing at 5 s; 20 machines syncing: ~9.7 GB/day of WAL plus the checkpoint copy, on the snapshotted ZFS dataset. Avoidable share estimated, not measured.
evidence: probe_report4.py: PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(PASSIVE) -> (0, 275, 275) after 40 reports from a truncated WAL; probe_report5.py statement list.
fix: IS NOT guards on the store_* NULL-setters and the auth/known-editor/token stamps (or coarsen those stamps to once a minute); skip replace_active_transfers when the set is empty and nothing is stored. Keep received_at as the liveness signal and the latch rule that an empty section deletes the row.

title: The self-diagnosis pass runs on every 15 s cycle and costs 18 write transactions and ~83 KB of WAL when nothing has changed
what: notices.run_checks runs at the end of every collector cycle (driven by the 15 s connections kind), commits once per check (17), re-asserts every open notice with an UPDATE plus an unused SELECT id, and rewrites the whole notice_last_checked JSON meta row ~28 times per pass with fresh timestamps nobody reads.
cost: ~7,900 cycles/day (sim_loop.py, default intervals). Per connections-only cycle measured: 18 commits, 29 upserts, 8 UPDATE, 80 SELECT, 83 KB WAL (vs ~8 KB the cycle needs). Per day ~140,000 write-lock acquisitions and ~650 MB WAL on the snapshotted ZFS /data dataset, each commit a lock api_report can queue behind. Same at 4 or 20 machines.
evidence: probe_notices.py: 17 commits / 28 INSERT / 95 KB WAL per pass; probe_cycle.py: 18 commits / 83,020 WAL bytes per cycle with a 15 s clock (12 KB with a frozen clock). ui.py:1912 is the only reader of notice_last_checked and uses only its key set.
fix: Run run_checks only when a kind other than connections ran, or at most every 60 s; keep check-evidence stamps in memory and write the meta row only when the set changes or every ~15 min; in db.notice skip the UPDATE when severity/body/fix are unchanged and last_seen is under ~10 min old. Keep one commit per check and leave a raising check's notices alone.

title: [ OK ] on WHAT THE SERVER CHECKS needs only that a kind was evaluated once, ever: a check that now raises every cycle, or a blind pass, still reads OK
what: The evidence map {kind: last_checked} persists across restarts and the panel only tests key presence, so once stamped a kind is [ OK ] for the life of the database; the timestamps are never read.
cost: A notice check that starts raising (import error after an update, bad row) is only logged and keeps showing [ OK ]; nothing tells anyone (alerts have check_failed, notices do not). The documented stale-stamp behaviour for file_move_detected on a blind inventory pass is not rendered anywhere, so a permanently blind inventory still shows hand-move detection [ OK ], the check whose silence turns moves into deletions (CR-267a).
evidence: Read the only consumer (ui.py:1912) and grepped every reference to NOTICE_CHECKS_META / notice_last_checked.
ledger: new (regression of the intent of resilience sweep 2026-08-28 fix pass finding 1 and dash-collector-alerts-1)
fix: Treat a stamp older than a per-kind bound (3x the writer's cadence, floor 1 h; 2x interval_inventory for file_move_detected) as NOT CHECKED with its age shown, and file a notice when a notice check raises, subject = the check name.

title: remoteneed deletes and re-inserts every unchanged missing-files list every minute
what: For every (folder, device) pair below 100 %, every 60 s, the pass fetches up to 3 pages of /rest/db/remoteneed then DELETEs and re-inserts up to 500 rows with a new refreshed_at whether or not the list changed. No wall-clock budget, unlike completion.
cost: Measured 0.12 MB WAL and 2 ms per pair per pass; 10 incomplete pairs = 1.09 MB/min = ~1.6 GB/day WAL while backlogs last, plus 1-3 remoteneed calls per pair per minute, each an index walk inside Syncthing (estimated tens of ms on a 20k-file folder). Scales with machines x projects behind.
evidence: probe_remoteneed.py: 1 pair 2 ms / 0.12 MB; 10 pairs 17 ms / 1.09 MB per 60 s pass. refreshed_at is read only by fetch_missing and the day-scale prune.
fix: Skip the fetch and rewrite for a pair whose need_items equals the value at its last fetch (force every ~15 min); when fetched, write only if (name, size) differs and otherwise bump refreshed_at with one UPDATE. Keep clear_missing_files for pairs that leave _incomplete and the poll-then-write order.

title: The inventory skip-signature is directory mtimes only, so a file caught mid-copy keeps its partial size and mtime until something else in that project changes
what: Directory mtime changes on create/remove/rename, not when a file grows in place. A walk during a copy written straight to its final name (Explorer/Finder/SMB card copy onto P:) records the partial size and mtime; afterwards the signature matches and the walk is skipped until another entry in that project changes, possibly never.
cost: nas_media size/mtime_ns is the hand-move identity key and the (basename, size) the companion's lane-B found-elsewhere test uses; a later hand move of that clip pairs nothing and is treated as a deletion on every machine (CR-267a re-upload + parked breaker). Project byte totals are short. Per-ingest probability is the overlap of a ~3-hourly walk with a 10-30 min copy: small per copy, recurring on shoot days.
evidence: Read _dir_signature (os.walk + os.stat(dirpath) per directory, no files) and the skip; POSIX/ZFS directory mtime semantics. Not reproduced on the NAS (read-only rule).
fix: After a walk, if any recorded file's mtime_ns is within ~30 min of walked_at, store an unsettled (NULL) signature so the next visit walks the files again. Keep the steady-state no-write skip and CR-297A's forced re-walk.

title: The 8-projects-per-cycle inventory window is spent on unchanged projects too, so 'is it on the server' lags 3 h today and ~16 h at 500 projects
what: The rotating cursor selects 8 projects per 900 s pass and only then compares each one's cheap signature, so an unchanged project consumes a slot; the cap meant to bound the expensive file walk also bounds the cheap check.
cost: Each project is visited every ceil(n/8) passes: 100 projects -> 3.1 h worst case (1.6 h average) before uploaded footage appears in nas_media (MEDIA PRESENCE, locate, hand-move pairing, proxy_pairs); 500 projects -> 15.6 h. replace_nas_media has no other caller.
evidence: Read _run_inventory and the defaults; grep shows the collector is the only refresher of nas_media.
fix: Signature-check all active projects (or a time-budgeted larger window) every pass and spend the 8-walk cap only on changed ones, oldest change first; optionally nudge inventory for a project named in a lane-A upload report. Keep walks before writes, the unmounted canary and the move limits.

title: Invariant 10 (proxy_pairs) re-reads every nas_media row of every project every 15 minutes even when no inventory changed
what: Every invariants pass loads all nas_media rows per active project and rebuilds the original/proxy sets, though the verdict can only change for projects whose inventory was replaced since the last pass.
cost: Measured 2.4 s for 200k rows and 1.58 s for 1M rows (desktop CPU; NAS slower) on the collector thread every 15 min; ~0.3-1 s today, ~8 s+ per pass at 500 projects x 10k files, during which connections/enforce wait.
evidence: probe_proxy_pairs.py: '100 projects x 10000 files = 1000000 rows: 1.58 s'.
fix: Cache each project's verdict in memory keyed on nas_inventory_state.walked_at (or tree_sig) and recompute only changed projects. Keep one subject per Proxy folder and the full found list CR-266c relies on.

title: Syncthing's pending-devices list is fetched on every cycle (~7,900 GETs a day) for a check whose threshold is 24 hours
what: run_cycle calls client.pending_devices() before every self-diagnosis pass, i.e. every 15 s, and its only consumer ignores devices pending less than 24 h.
cost: ~7,900 REST calls/day to the NAS Syncthing; while Syncthing is down each 15 s cycle also waits out the 10 s client timeout on this call.
evidence: probe_cycle.py: pending_devices 1.0 call per connections-only cycle.
fix: Fetch it only when the config kind ran this cycle or at most every 10 min and cache the answer, keeping 'could not ask -> None -> nothing cleared'. Folds into dash-collector-1 if run_checks moves to a slower cadence.
