The whole linux half now runs nowhere automatically while release_customers.py publishes --kind dashboard --make-current on 'ci.yml green', and the refusal text still claims those checks ran.
cost: The next customer release carrying a dashboard regression passes every automated gate; only the 24 h studio soak stands before every customer dashboard. The tools suite that pins publish_latest/publish_feed's own refusals no longer gates changes to them.
evidence: ci.yml:259-264; CI run 42837667812's linux job was red on dashboard pytest (460 s) - such a run now reads green; release_customers.py has no job-level check.
fix: Move linux to its own workflow or check JOB conclusions: windows+macos required for companion/onboard, linux 'success' (not 'skipped') required for --kind dashboard and release_customers.py; fix the refusal text. Fail closed when jobs cannot be read.

title: Pathway A builds a second, different binary of a commit CI already built; the studio soaks bytes no customer gets and one version names two binaries
what: Since 2026-11-10 CI builds the Windows exe for every main commit in ~3 min (tests_gate=ci). ship.cmd still builds locally and PUTs that build to the studio while the feed carries the CI build; PyInstaller output is not byte-reproducible.
cost: Per ship ~2 min of local PyInstaller/self-test plus ~3.5 min of suites CI already ran; the studio (policy=current) later meets the feed record for a version it holds with other bytes (409), and the studio soak vouches for bytes customers never receive.
evidence: Steps read; RELEASE_PATHWAYS step 3 notes A's make-current is undone by the feed poll; KNOWN_BUGS ~33279 records the same different-bytes mechanism for the dashboard bundle.
ledger: related to release-pipeline-6 (fixed); new for the companion path
fix: Step 2a downloads the CI artefact for HEAD and verifies it as publish_latest.verify does, requiring ci_green_for(sha); local build only behind -BuildLocally. Keep the clean-tree, version-free and Authenticode refusals.

title: The studio gets a feed release after up to a day plus ~14 min per 50 MB from GitHub's CDN; the 1.2 s direct PUT lives only in an off-repo scratchpad helper
what: Pathway B ends at the GitHub release; the studio learns of it on a daily poll (or a deliberate restart) and pulls every artefact over a ~60 KB/s NAS path. The owner's fast path (PUT the identical signed bytes over the tailnet) is a scratchpad helper with run id, sha and version retyped.
cost: Per release ~14 min per 50 MB artefact once the poll fires (feed/check 'past 15 min') vs 1.2 s for 54 MB by PUT, or up to 24 h with nothing; three releases on 2026-11-10.
evidence: Owner memory studio-package-direct-put.md (14 min / 50 MB vs 1.2 s / 54 MB, 2026-09-26) and ship-2026-09-25.md; the 86400 s poll default read in release_feed.py.
fix: publish_latest --studio <url>: after the feed publish, PUT the verified artefact with the exact signed record to /api/v1/admin/packages through build_editor_package's admin login (opt-in prompt). The bytes then equal the feed's. Keep the dashboard's signature check and REL-1 soak; never put the password on argv.

title: A companion ship means six hand edits of version strings (two companion copies, four installer copies forced every ship by SHIP-4)
where: companion/src/ccsync_companion/config.py + companion/pyproject.toml; installer/windows_bootstrap.ps1, onboarding/steps.py, installer/macos_bootstrap.sh, onboarding/build_onboard_macos.spec; tools/ship.ps1:475-507
what: pyproject.toml duplicates the companion version although setuptools can read it statically from config.py; the installer number has four copies, one checked only by a test; no tool writes them.
cost: 6 edits per pathway-A ship (three companion bumps on 2026-11-10), each a chance of a parity refusal after work has started (the 2026-08-10 .spec incident).
evidence: docs/RELEASE.md 'Where versions live'; companion/pyproject.toml uses setuptools>=68 with a literal version; git log shows the 0.9.89/0.9.90/0.9.91 bumps on 2026-11-10.
fix: tools/bump_version.py that rewrites every copy and runs the existing parity checks; dynamic = ["version"] with attr = ccsync_companion.config.VERSION in pyproject. Keep release.ps1's parity refusal.

title: publish_latest fails, and recommends --allow-red-ci, when CI on the newest build's commit is merely still running - the normal state for minutes after every push now
what: Release builds finish in ~2.5-3 min and ci.yml in ~5-6 min (12 with linux), so the newest green release run often sits on a commit whose CI is in progress; ci_green_for asks only --status success, cannot tell in-progress from red, and the refusal suggests the hotfix override. There is no wait and no fallback to the newest both-green commit.
cost: Each early run is a refusal plus an override hint, then a hand lookup of run ids, gh run watch, a re-run and a second passphrase prompt. Not unsafe (tests_vouched_by_ci still refuses) but it trains the habit the flag warns against.
evidence: Run timings: release-windows 15:46:48-15:49:40 (42847901698); CI windows job 5 m 52 s (42776015071); refusal text at :574-579.
fix: Query the ci.yml runs for the sha with their status; say 'in progress' and, with --wait, gh run watch it (and the release runs) before continuing. Red or unreadable still refuses.

title: The push-triggered release builds still install the dashboard venv, ffmpeg and rclone for a test run they skip
what: Those steps exist only for the suites; with run_tests empty on push the build runs -SkipTests / --skip-tests, and build.spec bundles neither rclone nor ffmpeg.
cost: Every push to main: ~55 s of a 172 s Windows build (32%: dashboard venv 23 s, ffmpeg 30 s, rclone 2 s) and ~33 s of a 150 s macOS build (22%), plus two third-party downloads that have broken builds before.
evidence: Step timings of runs 42847901698 and 42847901441; grep of companion/build.spec finds no rclone or ffmpeg.
fix: if: inputs.run_tests == true on the three steps in both workflows; a dispatched run_tests build keeps them.

title: CI runs twice per commit when a feature branch and main point at the same sha, and the publish gate accepts whichever run went green
what: push on branches '**' with a per-ref concurrency group starts two full matrices for one sha; with a flaky suite they can disagree, and ci_green_for passes if any run is green.
cost: On 2026-11-10 fabee82, 43a9e59, ffdf9f2 and 57eb0b2 each ran twice (20-29 min matrices at the time); 57eb0b2 was green on release-speed and red on main, and the green run vouches for main's publish. Minutes are free (public repo); the cost is runner queueing and a gate that re-run-until-green satisfies.
evidence: gh run list --workflow ci.yml with headBranch.
fix: Concurrency group keyed on github.sha for push events, or push only on main + pull_request; at least report a red sibling run.

title: The release docs and advisories still describe dispatch-only 36-minute builds and Mac-side publishing
what: The release workflows run on every push since 2026-11-10 and take ~3 min; docs/CI.md was updated, but RELEASE_PATHWAYS (the one-screen route for agents) and the workflow headers were not, and ship.ps1 still sends the owner to a Mac for the macOS companion that CI + publish_latest now produce.
cost: A session following RELEASE_PATHWAYS dispatches redundant builds (new bytes for the same commit) and budgets 36 min of waiting; ship's advisory sends the owner to a Mac.
evidence: The lines cited; docs/CI.md:232 already says both run on every push to main.
fix: Rewrite pathway B steps 2-3 as push + wait for the three runs on the sha; fix the workflow headers; make the ship 2c advisory name publish_latest.py --platform macos.

title: release-dashboard.yml is still dispatch-only while release_customers.py requires it green on the release sha
what: The other two release workflows moved to push-on-main; the 16 s dashboard bundle build did not, so a customer release needs a hand dispatch on the right commit, and re-dispatches create the different-bytes bundles KNOWN_BUGS records.
cost: One manual dispatch plus a run-id lookup per customer release; a re-dispatch after the studio applied a bundle breaks the byte match release_customers checks.
evidence: gh run list --workflow release-dashboard.yml: five runs, all workflow_dispatch, 13-17 s each.
fix: Add push: branches: [main] so each commit has exactly one bundle; it still never publishes.

title: The recipe's --mode image deletes and recreates the app on every Cards/Sorter deploy, which is the only reason the stale-digest trap exists
what: site.toml already has [stack] mode = image, so --mode image only adds the implied --recreate: the TrueNAS app is deleted and re-created from [stack] image. Without --mode the run takes the restart path, which keeps the live container and image, so no digest is needed. The docs' claim that a bare run rolls back is not what the code does.
cost: Every Cards/Sorter deploy pays an app delete+create instead of a restart (estimated 40-120 s extra downtime, ~4 extra SSH). A run with the digest omitted, mistyped or copied from site.toml (stale today: 0.7.78 vs 0.7.79 live) recreates the fleet dashboard on an older image.
evidence: Code path read end to end; site.toml [stack] read; CARDS_DEPLOY.md 2026-10-29 transcript shows 'deleted app for re-create' on a Cards-only run.
fix: Drop --mode image from the recipes now. In the script, read the live image with one docker inspect, refuse an image different from live unless --container-image is explicit and older than live unless --allow-older, recreate only when the rendered compose differs from the live config, and record the deployed digest. --mode still implies recreate for a real mode migration.

title: The premature health check FAILED is a fixed 10 s sleep followed by one probe, and on the recreate path it ends the run before the 150 s poll runs
what: verify_image_boot sleeps 10 s, reads docker logs, asks /api/v1/health once; a still-starting container fails it, the recreate path returns 1 immediately, and verify_dashboard_after_restart's deadline loop never runs. It also prints a --mode bind rollback instruction.
cost: Every recipe deploy on 2026-10-04 and 2026-10-29 ended in a false FAILED, exit 1 and a manual SSH docker ps; callers cannot tell it from a real failure. CI cold boot answers in 2.3 s (measured) but the NAS with its mounts takes longer than 10 s.
evidence: Code read; the doc's quoted FAILED line is line 2673 verbatim; CI smoke log timing.
fix: Poll health first with probe_dashboard_health's deadline, then read logs and /venv/.runtime-id once; print the bind rollback only if the boot line is still missing after the deadline.

title: In image mode the health gate demands the repo's dashboard VERSION, which an image-mode deploy never ships: 150 s of polling and exit 1 whenever the repo is ahead or an OTA bundle runs
what: verify_dashboard_after_restart requires version == repo VERSION, but push_code is False in image mode, so the live version is the image's or the OTA bundle's. A repo VERSION ahead of live makes the probe poll the full 150 s and print FAILED with a rollback for an app tree this mode never touched.
cost: 150 s and 30 SSH handshakes per Cards/Sorter deploy on the restart path whenever dashboard VERSION has been bumped but not released (the normal state between a dashboard commit and its OTA); the docs teach the operator to ignore exit 1.
evidence: Code read; CARDS_DEPLOY.md:241-245.
fix: In image mode read health once before the restart and expect that version; keep repo VERSION only when push_code is True.

title: Every remote command opens a new SSH connection: about 31 handshakes per deploy, plus one per health poll
what: run_ssh builds a fresh paramiko SSHClient, connects, password-authenticates, runs one command and closes. A recipe Cards deploy makes about 31; a restart-path deploy adds up to 30 more from the health poll.
cost: Estimated 0.5-1.5 s per connect+auth: 15-45 s per deploy, up to 45 s more on a slow poll.
evidence: Code read; count from main()'s path with sorter configured and --music-data none.
fix: Cache one connected client per process in run_ssh (reconnect on a dead transport), one channel per command; sudo password still on each channel's stdin, host-key pin checked once; reuse the transport for SFTP.

title: Every run re-ships BOTH Cards and Sorter trees, so each recipe needs the other tree's live commit read by hand, and the Cards recipe now ships Sorter master unpinned
what: ship_cards and ship_sorter are true whenever the site names a checkout, each from its default ref unless pinned. SORTER_DEPLOY has the operator read the live Cards sha by hand; CARDS_DEPLOY (written before the Sorter mount) passes no --sorter-commit, so it ships footage-sorter master. master equals the work branch today (abe2539), so harmless now.
cost: Per deploy an unneeded second tree: 5 SSH, SFTP of 57 or 479 files, two find walks, privileged cp -a + chown -R, rename, prune; plus one manual SSH step and a pasted sha. Failure: a Cards hotfix publishes an unfinished Sorter to /sorter, which moves real pool files.
evidence: Code read; git merge-base --is-ancestor in footage-sorter.
fix: Default each tree to keep-what-is-live: read both DEPLOYED_COMMIT markers in the start-of-run SSH and skip install_tree when the requested commit equals live; ship a tree only when its --*-commit is given. Fix CARDS_DEPLOY.md now to pass the live sorter sha.

title: The create-only host-dir step runs chown -R over all of <root>/data and <root>/venv on every deploy
what: The comment says data/ and venv/ contents are never touched on re-run; the command recursively re-owns both as root every time. In image mode venv is not mounted; /data holds dashboard.db, OTA trees, up to 8 GiB of backups, packages, Cards state.
cost: Recursive privileged metadata walk per deploy over a dataset measured at 23,135 entries / 12.9 GB (KNOWN_BUGS ~16106), estimated 1-5 s, plus a recursive mutation of the live DB directory on every Cards deploy; flips container-created 3000:3001 files to 3000:3000.
evidence: Code read against its own comment.
ledger: related to bug-hunt-2026-08-21 uid/gid finding (fixed); recursion not raised
fix: chown/chmod the top directory only; chown -R only when just created; skip <root>/venv in image mode.

title: Cards ships the whole MulticamPipeline commit minus a deny-list: 479 files where the mount needs about 160
what: work/ (198 files, 1.94 MB project working data), apps/ (Android source), legacy and 26 root scripts ship with the 156-file multicam_pipeline package. The Sorter already uses an allow-list. CARDS_DEPLOY.md says tests/ ships; the code excludes it.
cost: Per Cards deploy ~320 extra SFTP puts and ~3 MB, about two thirds of the upload's file count (estimated 5-10 s).
evidence: git ls-tree -l HEAD with the deploy's rules: 479 files / 8.45 MB shipped, multicam_pipeline 156 / 5.36 MB.
fix: Allow-list multicam_pipeline/ plus the root modules it imports (cards/config.py imports webtheme from the root; derive by an import test). Correct the tests/ paragraph in CARDS_DEPLOY.md.

title: Restart to pick up new vault data runs the full deploy and takes the whole dashboard down, when a restart or a per-episode close/open would do
where: CLAUDE.md (Deploying it ... or just a restart); E:\Projects\CLAUDE.md; dashboard/src/ccsync_dashboard/cards_pool.py:616-730; cards_landing.py:443-455
what: Both CLAUDE.md files send a vault-data refresh through the full Cards recipe. Engines are built per episode on open and the landing page already lets the occupant or an admin Close an episode; reopening rebuilds it from the vault.
cost: Each refresh costs ~31 SSH and an estimated 1-3 min of fleet-dashboard downtime vs 1 SSH and 20-60 s (docker restart) or zero downtime for Close/Open (which leaks three upstream threads per close, owner-accepted).
evidence: Code read of drop/_run_build; recipe text. Whether the library sweep re-reads the vault by itself was not checked (cards-library territory).
fix: Add a restart subcommand (docker restart + deadline health poll, no snapshot needed) and say in both CLAUDE.md files that one episode's new data needs only Close/Open.

title: A routine run docker pulls an image it will not run
what: Step 2h pulls [stack] image on every image-mode run including the restart path, which keeps the container's current image; with site.toml stale that is an older digest nothing starts.
cost: 1 SSH + registry round trip per run when cached; when pruned on the NAS, a 157 MB download (measured image size) on a 900 s timeout.
evidence: Code read; GHCR manifest size.
fix: Pull only when the run will create/recreate or the requested image differs from the live one.

title: A Cards or Sorter deploy runs the whole site provisioning and needs every secret to change one read-only directory
what: Only cards-web/sorter-web and a restart change, yet the run refuses without unrelated secrets, probes the uid, makes 8 provisioning SSH calls and re-renders the compose. main() is ~1,480 lines and is where SERVER-8, OPS-1/2/3 and server-tools-b-5 landed.
cost: Per Cards/Sorter deploy ~10 SSH connections of privileged commands that cannot affect the outcome (estimated 10-25 s) and a dependency on five unrelated secrets, which is why it only runs from creator-1's desktop session.
evidence: Code read.
fix: Subcommands sharing the existing helpers: cards/sorter (connect once, read live state, snapshot, install_tree for changed trees, docker restart, health poll against the pre-restart version), restart, and image --to <digest> with deploy-nas-1's guards; the full run stays for fresh installs and compose changes. Saves ~20 of ~31 SSH and the delete/create on the routine cases.

title: Every dashboard test migrates a fresh SQLite DB from schema v0
where: dashboard/tests/conftest.py:138 (`conn` fixture), and the ~300 `create_app(Settings(db_path=tmp_path/...))` call sites in 168 test files; `dashboard/src/ccsync_dashboard/db.py:2331` (`migrate`)
what: Each test builds a new DB and replays all ~60 migration steps (in `conn` or in the app lifespan), then boots the whole app. Migration is the largest single slice of per-test setup.
cost: Measured locally: `migrate` = 73 ms per fresh DB; `create_app`+lifespan = 98-110 ms on a fresh DB vs 29-45 ms on a pre-migrated copy, and the copy (`sqlite3.backup` from a session template) costs 6 ms. So ~65 ms saved per test locally. 3,950 of the 6,596 dashboard tests take 0.1-1 s on CI (sum 1,560 s of the 1,991 s total); CI's runner is ~2x slower than the base rig. Estimated: 3,900 x ~0.13 s = ~500 s CPU per CI run = ~125 s of the 529 s wall step on 4 workers, and ~4 min off a serial local run. At ~7 runs/day: ~15 min of linux-runner time per day (when the job is back on).
evidence: probe_app.py / probe_app2.py output: "fresh copy 0.000 app+lifespan 0.108 / premigrated copy 0.006 app+lifespan 0.032"; "migrate x20 avg 0.0727"; junit buckets 0.1-0.2 s: 380, 0.2-0.4: 1,477, 0.4-0.7: 1,465, 0.7-1: 425 tests.
fix: A session-scoped fixture migrates one template DB; `conn` and a `fresh_db(tmp_path)` helper copy it with `sqlite3.backup` (keeps WAL/user_version exact). Tests about migration itself (`test_db_migrations*`, anything passing `steps=`) keep the fresh path. Must not share one DB between tests (parallel rule in CLAUDE.md) - the copy is per test.
effort: M effort (call sites build Settings inline; a helper plus a sed-able pattern)

title: test_deploy_resilience opens a real socket to the studio NAS (site.toml 192.168.0.102) with TRUENAS_PW="pw"
what: `_real_run`'s docstring says "Nothing here opens a socket", but it stubs `run_ssh`/`install_tree`/provisioning and not the TrueNAS version note, which calls the real `truenas_api` against `site_value("nas","host")`. A module global (`_VERSION_NOTE_PRINTED`) makes only the FIRST real-run test per process pay it, so the cost lands on whichever test runs first.
cost: CI: `test_a_step_3_query_failure_restarts_the_container` = 30.0 s (the connect timeout), the slowest server test and 38% of the 78 s suite sum; base rig: 21 s (Windows' SYN-retry give-up; the NAS did not answer on :443 during my run). On any machine where the NAS IS reachable on 443 (a LAN editor box, or TRUENAS_WS_URL set), the suite performs a real JSON-RPC login to the production NAS with password "pw" - a failed-auth event in the NAS log and a step towards its login throttle, from a test. Once per server-suite run (every CI run, every `ship.cmd`, which gates on this suite).
evidence: faulthandler dump at 8 s: `truenas_rpc.py:158 __init__ <- _open_ws <- rest_call <- common.py:1694 truenas_api <- common.py:2277 print_truenas_version_note <- install_dashboard_app.py:6164 main <- test_deploy_resilience.py:324 _real_run`. site.toml:3 `host = "192.168.0.102"`. junit: 30.0 s on CI.
fix: In `_real_run`, `monkeypatch.setattr(ida, "print_truenas_version_note", lambda *a, **k: "")`; better, a server/tests conftest autouse fixture that makes `socket.create_connection` to any non-loopback address raise, so the next unstubbed path fails in 0 s instead of reaching a NAS. Saves 30 s per server-suite run.

title: Three SYNC-3 express tests each stall 10 s and now pass via a timed-out fake spawn
what: The fake "periodic child" blocks INSIDE the Popen factory, which runs under `_proc_lock` (the deliberate spawn-and-publish lock, KNOWN_BUGS B13). Since the 2026-09-26 handoff work, `_express_partition` calls `handoff_inflight_paths()`, which takes `_proc_lock` - so every flush waits until the factory's `release.wait(10)` times out and raises in the background thread. The tests then pass against a periodic run that FAILED, not one in flight.
cost: 3 x 10.0 s on Windows and on macOS every CI run (30 s summed per OS, ~60 s per run) and on every local companion run; ~7 CI runs/day = ~7 min/day of runner time. Worse: the scenario no longer matches the docstring, so a regression in "express defers while a periodic child is running" (where the child has spawned and the lock is free) is not what these tests exercise.
evidence: faulthandler at 5 s: thread A in `test_rclone_lane_races.py:846 factory <- rclone_lane.py:6486 _run_popen`; main thread in `rclone_lane.py:3678 _live_handoffs <- 3685 handoff_inflight_paths <- 7351 _express_partition <- 7254 _express_flush_inner <- test:171 _flush_now`. junit: 10.0 / 10.0 / 11.0 s (Windows), 10.0-10.1 s (macOS).
ledger: new (related to B13, which stays as is)
fix: Return the `_FakeProc` immediately and make its `wait()`/`poll()` block on `release` (the child is running, the spawn is over), which is what the test means and frees `_proc_lock`. Do not loosen the B13 lock in production.

title: The companion and dashboard suites run serially in run_all_tests.ps1
what: CLAUDE.md (2026-11-10) says to run the two big suites with `-n auto` (dashboard `--dist loadfile`) and quotes ~1 min vs ~10 and ~2.5 vs ~19; CI does so, but the one script CLAUDE.md names for "everything at once" passes no `-n`, and `-Changed` scoped runs inherit the same.
cost: Every local full gate costs ~29 min for those two suites instead of ~3.5 (CLAUDE.md's own measurements): ~25 min per local run. The memory notes record a full local gate after each fix pass; at even one a day that is ~2 h/week of wall time on the base rig, which also runs the live companion.
evidence: grep of run_all_tests.ps1 finds no `-n`, `xdist` or `loadfile`; xdist 3.8.0 is installed in both venvs (`import xdist` from the dashboard venv) and is in both locks.
fix: Add per-suite extra args to the suite table: companion `-n auto`, dashboard `-n auto --dist loadfile`; leave the 11 small suites serial (each is under 70 s and xdist start-up would eat the gain). Keep `server/` serial and through bash.

title: CI runs the full matrix for duplicate pushes, docs-only commits and an unchanged nightly SHA; select_suites.py is not wired in
where: .github/workflows/ci.yml:30-47 (`push: branches: ["**"]`, `schedule`, `concurrency: ci-${{ github.ref }}`); tools/select_suites.py (used only by run_all_tests.ps1 -Changed)
what: Concurrency is per ref, so one SHA pushed to `main` and a feature branch runs twice; the nightly schedule re-runs main even when that SHA already has a green push run; there is no `paths-ignore`, so a docs-only commit (e.g. this audit's files) runs every suite; `select_suites.py`'s docstring promises "the shape CI's per-push plan will use" but ci.yml never calls it.
cost: In the last 30 runs: 57eb0b2 ran 3x (main push, release-speed push, nightly), fabee82/43a9e59/ffdf9f2 2x each (main + sorter-module), dd084b6 and 1bc7ede 2x (push + nightly), 93d3253 nightly 2x on consecutive days with no new commit: ~9 of 30 runs (30%) re-tested a SHA already tested. At ~7 runs/day that is ~2 redundant full runs/day = ~2 x (windows ~6-15 min + macos ~5-11 min, and macOS minutes bill at 10x on private repos) = ~25-50 runner-minutes/day, plus queue time in front of the run that matters (run 42837667812 took 3,450 s end to end for ~800 s of job time).
evidence: `gh run list --workflow ci.yml -L 30` and `gh run view --json jobs` (timings above).
fix: (a) `push: branches: [main]` plus `pull_request`, or a `concurrency` group keyed on `github.sha` for push events; (b) nightly job's first step exits 0 if `gh run list --commit $SHA --status success` already has a green ci.yml run (publish_latest still finds a green run for that SHA); (c) `paths-ignore: ['docs/**', '**/*.md']` on push, keeping CLAUDE.md-cited docs that tests read (check `test_test_map.py`'s path-literal audit first). Do not skip-by-select_suites in CI until M2's "last full green" base exists - its own fail-closed rules need that base.
risk: low risk for (a)/(b), medium for (c) (some tests read docs)

title: With the linux job off, a green CI run gates no dashboard, server or web suite
what: `publish_latest.py` and `release_customers.py` publish "the newest GREEN ci.yml run"; since today that run contains the companion, onboarding, bench and installer suites only. The dashboard (6,596 tests), server (944, the deploy-script guard), broll/web, music/web, ytdl/web, broll/indexer, tools suites, the CRLF gate, the licence gate for the container and the notices check now run nowhere automatically. The owner's reason was flakiness and wall time, both of which -1, -7 and -2 here reduce.
cost: A dashboard regression or a CRLF `run.sh` (which once took the dashboard down) reaches a green CI run and the vendor feed's provenance with nothing red. Image builds (image.yml) still ship the dashboard.
evidence: ci.yml:259-264 and its comment; run 42847901497 (d20af6a) completed in 17 s.
ledger: related to the owner decision of 2026-11-10 (d20af6a)
fix: Cheaper way to keep the guarantee without holding companion releases: re-enable the job with `continue-on-error: true` (it reports, does not hold publish_latest) and keep the cheap steps (CRLF gate, licence gate, server suite, the small web suites, ~4 min total) blocking; restore the dashboard step to blocking once -1/-7 land. Do not touch the owner's choice to unblock companion releases.

title: Six dashboard tests sit exactly on the 10 s SQLite busy_timeout on CI
where: dashboard/tests/test_presence.py:19 (`env`), dashboard/tests/test_multi_machine.py (`env`), tests `test_presence::test_prune_completion_not_shared` (10.2 s), `test_multi_machine::test_adopt_onto_the_same_computers_own_empty_row_is_allowed` (10.2 s), `::test_adopt_renamed_machine_refuses_a_taken_name` (10.1 s), `test_dashboard_update::test_a_wedged_dashboard_leaves_the_boot_counter_standing` (10.3 s); `db.connect` busy_timeout (db.py:714)
what: These fixtures open a second connection with `dbmod.connect(db_path)` while the app's lifespan is live inside `TestClient`; a test that writes through that connection waits out the full busy_timeout behind a lifespan writer, then proceeds. Locally the same tests take well under 1 s, so it depends on how slow the runner is.
cost: ~41 s summed per CI dashboard run; the same shape on a slower or busier runner is "database is locked" at 10 s, i.e. a test that fails "a different pair each run" - the exact symptom for which the linux job was switched off today (test_smoke_boot, test_cards_edit, test_cli_tools were named; these are the same class).
evidence: junit run 42804473185: four tests at 10.1-10.3 s plus two more at >= 9.5 s; all < 1 s in local single-file runs of test_presence / test_multi_machine (not re-run here: estimated from the 10.0 s quantisation).
fix: Have these fixtures write their seed rows BEFORE entering `TestClient` (the app then boots onto a seeded DB), or wait for a lifespan "boot writes done" event before yielding; identify the lifespan writer that holds the lock (collector first cycle is the likely one) with `CCSYNC`-style logging on CI.

title: A one-off ~35 s stall per process on the macOS runner
where: companion tests `test_broll_server::test_status_over_http` (35.5 s mac / 0.5 s win), `test_field_review_paths::test_the_guard` (35.5 / 0.5), `test_lane_watchdog::test_the_media_tree_loop_stamps_a_heartbeat` (35.0 / 0.0), onboarding `test_legal_steps::test_the_identity_token_does_not_follow_a_redirect` (36.0 / 1.0)
what: Exactly one test per pytest process (three companion xdist workers + the serial onboarding run) pays ~35 s on macOS only; the first two and the onboarding one start a stdlib `ThreadingHTTPServer`, whose `server_bind` calls `socket.getfqdn(host)` - a reverse lookup that is slow on GitHub's macOS image. Every later test in the same process is fast.
cost: ~140 s summed per CI run; ~35 s of the macOS job's ~200-530 s companion step plus ~36 s of its 47 s onboarding step. ~7 runs/day = ~16 macOS runner-minutes/day (billed at 10x).
evidence: junit Windows-vs-macOS deltas: the only four tests with a > 2 s mac-only delta are these, all 35.0-36.0 s. The getfqdn mechanism is inferred, not traced on a Mac.
fix: In companion and onboarding conftest, a session autouse fixture that resolves once (`socket.getfqdn("127.0.0.1")`) to confirm, then override `server_bind` in `BrollCompanionServer`/`FieldHTTPServer` to set `server_name` without `getfqdn` (see OUT OF TERRITORY: the same call runs at tray start on an editor's Mac).

title: Fixed real sleeps pinned in two run.sh tests and one rclone test
where: dashboard/tests/test_run_sh_restart_loop.py:253 (50.1 s, pays run.sh:321's 5/15/30 s retry sleeps "deliberately"), :350 (12.0 s, `STUB_NIGHTLY_SLEEP="12"`); companion/tests/test_rclone_filters.py:1644 (30.2 s win / 30.1 s mac: a deliberately failing rclone run under production `--retries 3 --retries-sleep 10s`, rclone_lane.py:2346)
what: The behaviour pinned is "gives up cleanly after 4 attempts" and "rclone reads a blank line as the root dir", not the wall time of the waits.
cost: ~62 s on the dashboard suite (one worker's critical path under loadfile) and ~30 s on each companion OS, every run: ~2 min summed per CI run, ~14 min/day.
evidence: junit timings above; run.sh:321 `for unblock_delay in 5 15 30 0`.
fix: run.sh reads its retry delays from an env var defaulting to "5 15 30 0" (the test sets "0 0 0 0"; still asserts attempts=4); the nightly test can use 3 s with the >8 s assertion scaled; append `--retries 1` to the express argv in the blank-line test (it asserts rclone's parse, not retries).
risk: low risk (run.sh change ships in the image, defaults unchanged)

title: The Cards gate runs every kind and every python suite one at a time
where: MulticamPipeline (Editing tree) tests/run_all.py:1091 (`--jobs` default 1), :1192 (python half always sequential), SUITES table :123
what: The SUITES table's own measured seconds sum to 753 s (116 suites), of which BROWSER_AGENT 357 s, PYTHON 135 s, BROWSER_PERF 133 s, OWN 92 s; the rest of the owner's ~25 min is per-kind server boots, the 20 s SETTLE pauses and untimed suites. `--fast` keeps the 281 s of suites under 15 s and drops every perf suite, every encode/settle suite and the six slowest browser suites (test_looks 112 s, test_ui_pass 66 s, test_edit_view 45 s, ...).
cost: With `--jobs 3` the browser half is bounded by its largest kind (~357 s + its boot) instead of the sum (~620 s + all boots): estimated ~4-5 min off a 25 min gate; the two perf kinds (133 s) judge timings and are skewed by running beside anything, so they are better as a separate `--group perf` step than inside the merge gate. Gate runs are per Cards deploy (the memory index records roughly one a day in busy weeks).
evidence: SUITES table parsed (rows/secs above); argparse default `--jobs 1`; not measured end to end (the gate must not be run in this audit).
fix: Default the gate to `--jobs 3` (one server per kind is already built for it) and move `perf` out of the default full gate into its own invocation; keep the SETTLES suites serial. Measure once before changing the default.
risk: medium risk (parallel kinds share the box with Resolve tests' timings)

title: Waveform peaks: one unbounded thread + ffmpeg per clip, each buffering the whole decoded clip in the dashboard process
what: With no fleet set in the dashboard mount, peaks_state starts a thread per distinct clip with no cap; each decodes the whole clip to s16le via communicate() and widens it to int32. Failures are not recorded, so the page's ~10 retries over 120 s each re-decode.
cost: Measured per clip: 64 min ~307 MB transient, 120 min ~576 MB. A lane opening on 12 hour-long multicams without .peaks is 4-7 GB at once inside the uvicorn process that serves fleet status; recurs after every re-render.
evidence: probe.py: 61 MB stdout + 246 MB numpy peak (64 min), 115 + 461 MB (120 min); code read; FLEET.md section 12 says the page's peaks path is thread-per-file.
fix: Queue peaks on the existing single lite/src worker and stream the decode in fixed chunks (max-pool per chunk); record failures per (wav, mtime). Keep first-writer-wins, the PK rate header, ETag/304.

title: ProjectAgentEngine runs LibraryEngine.__init__ twice: orphan GoogleTranslator thread + cache per engine, every store read twice
where: MulticamPipeline cards/project_agent.py:115-121; cards/agent.py:66; cards/project_engine.py (ProjectEngine.__init__ -> LibraryEngine.__init__); cards/library_engine.py:419-423, 535-536; cards/translate.py:199-225
what: Diamond construction calls LibraryEngine.__init__ via AgentLink and again via ProjectEngine. The first GoogleTranslator's worker thread is already running and keeps that translator and its parsed cache alive forever with no handle to stop it.
cost: Per engine: +1 thread, +1 in-memory copy of gt_translations.json (estimated a few MB), and double build-time reads of timeline_plans.json (3.4 MB on Civil Defence), notes, place, colours over the vault mount.
evidence: Code read: translate.py:225 starts the worker inside __init__.
ledger: related to PL-RES-77 / bug-dash-jobs-cards-4 (open); this part is new
fix: Make LibraryEngine.__init__ re-entry safe, or stop the first translator before the second init. Keep the write_allow/media_map resets ProjectAgentEngine relies on.

title: A cooperative stop is cheap: ProjectAgentEngine.stop skips LibraryEngine.stop and _lib_worker has no exit
what: Only the library sweep loop and the translator ignore stop; every other worker is flag-aware, drains and exits, or is one-shot. About 10 lines (call LibraryEngine.stop, while not self._stop in _lib_worker, wake it, close the reader) would make engines releasable.
cost: Today each dropped engine leaks per PL-RES-77 (+128 MB, 15 threads); with this fix plus cards-library-2 the pool could evict instead of refuse.
evidence: Code read; LibraryEngine.stop docstring says ProjectAgentEngine.stop does not reach it.
fix: ProjectAgentEngine.stop: set _stop, LibraryEngine.stop(self), _lib_wake.set(), reader.close(); loop on not _stop; drop ring/gz/tokens caches. Pinned jobs still finish.

title: Publish ring keeps 32 full copies of every card dict (~57 MB at 1,522 cards); frames cache duplicates token lists
what: build_state makes fresh card dicts every build, so each of the RING_KEEP=32 entries is a full card set. _frames_cache stores a converted tuple copy of every clip's tokens.
cost: Measured 1.77 MB/version -> 57 MB per engine after 32 bumps on a 1,522-card cut; frames cache +2.0 MB per hour-long interview (about 18 MB for 9). Most of the measured +128 MB per engine.
evidence: probe.py ring; probe2.py frames (2.0 MB vs 0.26 MB as two array('d')).
fix: Keep per-card fingerprints (or last 8 versions) in the ring instead of dicts; store starts/ends as array('d') and index into entry tokens. Keep state_delta patch semantics and first_of_seq.

title: timeline_plans.history.jsonl appends the whole op list per rev: quadratic, never pruned, never read
what: PlanStore._put appends a line with all current ops on every append/undo/mode change.
cost: Measured 70.3 MB for one 400-op insert draft (plans file 340 KB); estimated 10-15 MB for 400 trims/moves; per episode, forever, in the vault and its snapshots.
evidence: probe.py plan section; PROJECT-FORMAT-PLAN.md row 5.
fix: Append deltas only (full list only when ops shrink) and rotate at a size cap.

title: timeline_place.json rewritten whole, indented, ~1/s per device while the lane plays
what: The moving lane head re-arms a 1 s place save; the server dumps every timeline's record (up to 24 devices, 50 marks, no timeline eviction) each time.
cost: Measured 1.41 MB / 46.7 ms per save at an upper-bound 100 timelines x 24 devices; realistic 50-300 KB estimated; 1 vault write/s per playing device for hours.
evidence: probe.py place section; page code read.
fix: Skip head-only saves during playback (save on pause or every 15 s), compact JSON, evict timelines untouched for 90 days.

title: NoteStore and BinStore unlocked with one fixed .tmp: concurrent saves can raise or corrupt; a corrupt file loads as empty
what: set() on HTTP threads and heal() on the publish/edit thread both json.dump self.data to path+'.tmp' with no lock; RuntimeError is uncaught and two writers can interleave into invalid JSON, which the next load reads as {}.
cost: Rare, but the outcome is every note, stack mark and collapsed state of the episode silently lost.
evidence: Code read; PlanStore/PlaceStore do take a lock.
fix: Lock mutate+snapshot, unique tmp names, set a bad file aside on load instead of overwriting it.

title: Extraction/proxy failures are sticky for the engine's life, even across a root switch
what: _src_fail/_vid_fail record any failure, transient or not, and nothing clears them.
cost: One NAS hiccup or timeout keeps a clip dark on every editor's lane until the dashboard container restarts (weeks).
evidence: Code read.
fix: Store (why, time, src mtime); retry after ~10 min or on mtime change; keep 'no audio track' sticky.

title: Library sweep polls Postgres every 2 s forever, 4 round trips per tick, with or without viewers
what: _lib_worker wakes every 2 s for the container's life; live-on-library it runs a 4-query fingerprint; file mode still wakes and may run _library_default queries every 30 s.
cost: ~2 queries/s = ~173k/day per engine against the project library server, including nights.
evidence: Code read.
fix: One-query fingerprint; back off to 30 s when no api/state was served in 2 min, wake on the next poll.

title: Undo of an in-place library edit is two transactions; failure between them half-restores the timeline; backups never pruned
what: restore() commits the deletion of created rows, then re-inserts and updates in a second transaction; every apply and dry run writes a backup JSON nothing prunes.
cost: A failed second transaction leaves the timeline without the edit's items and without the originals; mitigated by the REAL_LIBRARIES gate (lab libraries only since 2026-09-29).
evidence: Code read; undo's docstring says the restore has already committed.
fix: Do delete + re-insert + update in one transaction on one connection; prune old backups keeping the latest per timeline.

title: remote_audio caches never pruned; crashed encodes leave .tmp files
what: Opus copies, extractions, .peaks and 480p proxies accumulate per clip name forever; renamed clips orphan theirs; a kill mid-encode leaves .tmp* files.
cost: Estimated 0.5-0.7 GB per footage hour for 480p proxies once the video window is used, 20-30 MB/h for audio; unreported.
evidence: Code read; no prune path exists.
fix: At engine start delete *.tmp* older than a day and report remote_audio size on the health line; optional age eviction of unserved proxies.

title: LibraryReader holds one open transaction on Resolve's live project library for the life of the process
where: MulticamPipeline: multicam_pipeline/library/library_reader.py:411-436; kept alive by multicam_pipeline/cards/agent.py:686-696 and polled by agent.py:1020-1029 every 2 s
what: psycopg2 begins a transaction on the first execute; _query never commits, rolls back or sets autocommit, and the connection is cached forever, so each reader sits idle-in-transaction holding AccessShareLocks on every table it has read.
cost: Every NAS engine (up to 2) and agent/project server, for days. Can hold back xmin (table bloat in the tables Resolve saves into) and makes any ACCESS EXCLUSIVE request (Resolve library schema upgrade, VACUUM FULL, restore DDL) block, with every later Resolve query queued behind it.
evidence: No commit/rollback/autocommit in library_reader.py; the sibling ProjectDatabase was fixed for exactly this on 2026-09-03 (multicam_transcripts.py:184-191: an idle reader pinned the server's xmin for hours).
ledger: new (same defect as the 2026-09-03 ProjectDatabase fix)

title: The 10 Hz loop serialises the whole state twice every tick whether or not anything changed or anyone watches
what: Every 0.1 s tick runs _summary_state/_sections (markers x cards), a json.dumps of cards+markers for the change key, and a full json.dumps of the ~680 KB state, though cards change at most once per 1 s sweep and only the playhead moved.
cost: Measured 3.7 ms per tick on a real 487-card state = 37 ms CPU/s (3.7% of a core) and ~13 MB/s of garbage strings, all day beside Resolve, page open or not; linear in cards.

fix: On playhead-only ticks skip summaries/key dump and splice the playhead into the cached body; keep the rule that a playhead move never bumps version.

title: Full 1 Hz sweep (~1,350 RPCs under the shared API lock) runs with no page open and during playback
what: uid+start+duration per V1 item every second plus markers and a bridge.sweep_items call; nothing reduces the cadence when no browser polls the page, and nothing pauses it while the playhead moves.
cost: Repo's own measurement: 135-141 ms of Resolve's single scripting thread per sweep at 451 items (~14% of its capacity), held under the lock the companion tray shares; most of the day nobody has /cards open.
evidence: Loop code; LAG-INVESTIGATION.md section 4 table and 2026-08-31 note.
fix: Server reports viewers on /agent/state (and the tunnel in the companion role); with none, sweep every 10 s and read the playhead at 1 s; skip the full sweep while the playhead advances. Edits/jumps still force an immediate sweep.

title: bridge.sweep_items() is called every second even when every item's detail is cached
where: MulticamPipeline: multicam_pipeline/cards/resolve_engine.py:482 (used only on a miss at 489-493)
what: The library rows only feed _detail_from_row, which returns the cache when uid and dur are unchanged, but the read is made first; in the companion role it is wait_while_menu_open + 4 head RPCs under _API_LOCK + a possible Postgres read.

title: Library conform passes allow_open=True after proving the project closed, disabling the writer's lock gate for the race it exists for

title: DB writer's real-library protection is a hard-coded denylist of five names

title: Agent never re-binds its project database after the editor switches library

title: Agent uploads the whole ~680 KB state uncompressed on every version change
what: Each edit/translation/marker version change is a new HTTP connection with the full state plus every clip ever met, no Content-Encoding.
cost: 678 KB vs 131 KB gzipped (8 ms); ~270 ms vs ~60 ms on a 20 Mbit/s uplink on the edit-confirm path; ~136 MB vs ~26 MB per 200 edits/hour.
evidence: gzip probe on scratch/state8802.json.
fix: gzip the push and accept Content-Encoding gzip on /agent/state in the handler and the dashboard tunnel; server first.

title: Cut-list history grows without bound as full uncompressed copies in the vault
what: Each edit writes the full previous file to Cuts/.history and lists the shared folder; beyond the newest 200, every 10th revision is kept forever.
cost: 198 KB per 433-cut list: 2,000 revisions -> 380 files / 75 MB, 10,000 -> 1,180 files / 234 MB per cut list on the NAS vault, plus a growing per-edit SMB listdir.
evidence: probe_cut.py (loads 2.6 ms, dumps 1.1 ms, gzip 54 KB) and the retention arithmetic.
fix: Thin by age beyond 200 (hourly for a week, daily after) and gzip old revisions; keep the oldest.

title: project_pick.doc_save is an unlocked read-merge-write through one fixed .tmp name
what: Two HTTP threads of one engine can both read, both write cards_pick.json.tmp, and lose a key or fail the replace (only printed).
cost: Rare; a lost pick or last-project entry, so the page reopens on the wrong cut list after a restart.
evidence: Code.
ledger: related to ccsync CLAUDE.md engine-pool note
fix: Module lock around load-merge-write and a unique temp name.

title: ripple_keys.ahk checks the foreground window once per batch, by process, not per key
what: WinActive on ahk_exe Resolve.exe passes for any Resolve window including a modal; keys are sent 100 ms apart with no re-check; BlockInput likely inert unelevated; keystroke edits do not run the GetCurrentPage dialog check the conform has.
cost: Rare; a Resolve popup mid-batch receives the remaining keys, which a timeline rollback does not undo.
evidence: Script and _keys/_park code.
fix: Re-check the main window before each key and abort the batch on change; add the GetCurrentPage dialog check at the top of _apply_edit.

title: Every warm edit-chat turn re-sends a ~46k-character digest of the whole cut list, and the conversation keeps every copy
what: A warm turn's CURRENT STATE still carries one line per known card with the first 60 characters of its words. At 500 cards that is 46,378 characters (104 KB), only 32% smaller than the full digest, and each copy stays in the provider conversation.
cost: About 35-45k fresh input tokens per chat message at 500 cards (estimated), plus about 400k tokens of history after ten turns, re-read every turn. The context window can be approached within a handful of turns on top of a ~322k-char corpus.
evidence: probe_digest.py: full 67,750 chars / 165,802 bytes, compact 46,378 chars / 104,286 bytes. _turn builds digest(engine, known) on every turn.
fix: Send known cards as [uid] person dur with no words, or only the cards changed since rev_seen plus a bare uid order. Keep highlights and the uid-rename resend property.

title: The 1.67 MB page goes out in full on every load: no validator, and the gzip is redone for each request
what: render_page caches the text, but _send gzips 1.67 MB on every request and sends no ETag or Cache-Control. The service worker's navigation arm is network-first and never caches it.
cost: About 35 ms of dashboard CPU and 557 KB on the wire per load, reload, pop-out window or phone open. A 304 is never possible.
evidence: Measured: doc 1,667,928 B; gzip level 5 32.7 ms giving 557,530 B; encode 1.07 ms; _sig 0.52 ms.
fix: Cache (bytes, gzip, etag=page_version()) per sig, and send ETag + Cache-Control: no-cache with a 304 on If-None-Match. Bytes are unchanged, so the golden test still holds.

title: Every pop-out panel window runs its own state poll loop
what: poll() starts unconditionally in every window, panel windows included, at 600 ms remote / 250 ms local. There is no visibility gating, and the BroadcastChannel carries only selection and playhead.
cost: Main window + 2 pop-outs + phone = about 6.7 requests/s per editor through the login gate, a2wsgi and engine.tick(), for as long as the windows are open.
evidence: Read: top-level poll() call, and PANEL never stops it.
fix: Panel windows take the main window's state over the channel, with a fallback poll; or slow polling while hidden. Keep the fast PENDING confirm.

title: Every Claude JSON turn leaves a temp directory and answer file that nothing deletes
what: Seven mkdtemp(prefix=timeline_cards_*) sites and no rmtree. _run_claude_json reads the answer and leaves the file.
cost: One directory per chat turn, search or describe, and about 50-60 per shortening pass, in container /tmp until the next recreate or in %TEMP% for good.
evidence: grep: mkdtemp in 7 places, rmtree in none.
fix: rmtree the answer's parent directory in a finally block in _run_claude_json, only when its name starts with timeline_cards_.

title: The transcript-search corpus re-walks the episode tree six times to answer one /api/search/scopes
what: corpus() re-lists every person and clip folder and stats every transcript on every call, and one scopes answer calls it 6 times.
cost: 15 people / 200 clips: 1,291 stats + 1,302 listdirs, 58 ms locally per modal open or scope change. Over SMB (standalone PC server) about 1-2.5 s (estimated), linear in clips.
evidence: probe_tsearch.py with wrapped os.stat/os.listdir.
fix: Memoise the signature for about 2 s, or pass one corpus through state/_expects. The hash semantics are unchanged.

title: A failed whisper corpus run leaves its scratch folder in %TEMP%
what: The scratch directory (run.json, .turns: MB of JSON) is removed only at the end of the success path, and run_worker raises when the worker fails.
cost: Each failed or retried transcribe on a GPU machine leaves MBs to tens of MBs that nothing prunes.
evidence: Read: no try/finally.
fix: try/finally: shutil.rmtree(scratch, ignore_errors=True).

title: The two translation caches only ever grow, one entry per distinct text a cut has ever had
what: Keys are the exact cut text, so every trim, split or extend variant adds an entry that is never pruned. Every save is a whole-file read-merge-rewrite of a vault file shared by two processes.
cost: Estimated 0.5-5 MB per episode over a long edit. Each save and each cross-process refresh then parses the whole file (tens of ms).
evidence: Read: no pruning path.
fix: On save, drop old entries whose key is not a current card's key. Never drop the keys of live cards.

title: The edit view rebuilds every row by innerHTML on every new state version
where: MulticamPipeline multicam_pipeline/cards/page/09-edit.js:108-109 and :147-150 (edvBuild), reached from 01-state.js:4274 (paintList -> laneDraw(true) -> edvDraw -> edvBuild)
what: edvBuild's cache key includes `CARDS` by identity, and render() assigns a fresh `CARDS=LIVE` array on every version, so any version bump (an edit confirm, every translate answer, a note, another device's edit) throws away all rows and rebuilds them with `EDLIST.innerHTML=rows.map(edvRowHtml).join('')`. The card list beside it got a keyed patch on 2026-09-03; the edit view never did.
cost: measured at 500 cards with the edit view open: 500 rows = 5,000 nodes including 1,000 `<canvas>` elements, rebuilt on 10 of 10 version bumps; render() goes from 5.7 ms (edit view shut, 3 DOM mutations for a one-card change) to 23.2 ms on the desktop. Estimated 90-140 ms per version on a phone at the repo's 4-6x CPU factor - and the edit view is the phone's main view (GOTCHAS section 22). A 91-card translate run republishes per answer, so that is ~91 full rebuilds; every edit costs one, on top of the waveform canvases each row must redraw.
evidence: probe2-out-500.json `edv` {rows 500, nodes 5000, canv 1000} and `edvBump` {rebuilds 10/10, rebuildMsAvg 4.6 (the innerHTML alone), renderMsAvg 23.2} vs probe-out-500.json `oneChange` {renderMs 5.7, mutations 3}.
ledger: new (LANE-ZOOM-PERF-INVESTIGATION section 10 fixed the shorten panel's forced `edvBuild(true)`, not this path)
fix: key edvBuild on what the rows DRAW (LSEG identity already changes only when laneModel rebuilds; or a per-row signature like cardItems' `stable` string) and patch rows by uid as patchList does, re-using each row's element and canvas; only `top`, number and the changed row need writing. Must keep EDKEY's existing invalidations (zoom, width, language, shorten removals) and the `cur` row bookkeeping (EDCUR reset).

title: An unchanged poll still repaints the whole lane canvas and walks every card row
what: every poll whose version did not move calls hilite(), which unconditionally asks for a full `laneDraw` (and through it `edvDraw`) and removes/re-adds `.ph` on every child of #list, even when PH and PHUID are what they were last time. The poll runs every 600 ms on the NAS-served page (REMOTE) and keeps running in a hidden tab (no visibilitychange gate in 08-places.js; Chrome throttles it to 1/s, then 1/min after 5 minutes hidden).
cost: measured: 8 polls -> 8 full lane redraws in 5 s with nothing changing (1.6 Hz); hilite 0.19 ms over 500 rows, laneDraw 0.15 ms headless without peaks, ~1.2-1.4 ms with real peaks at 80 clips and 7-8 ms at CPU x4 (take five's table). Per open tab that is a full-canvas GPU raster + composite 1.6 times a second all day, on the machine whose Chrome shares an iGPU with Resolve; small per tick, but it is pure waste and it also keeps the GPU process from idling.
evidence: probe-out-500.json `idleDraws` {fullDrawsIn5s 8, pollsIn5s 8, REMOTE true}, `hiliteMs` 0.19.
fix: in hilite (or at the poll's `else` branch) skip when PH, PHUID and the list's version are unchanged since the last hilite, and keep a reference to the previous `.ph` element instead of sweeping all children. Optionally stretch the poll to a few seconds while `document.visibilityState==='hidden'` (15-offline.js already re-asks on visible). Must not break follow (laneFollowTick needs the call when FOLLOW is on and the card has drifted - keep that branch).

title: The spoken-word highlight rewrites the playhead card's innerHTML on every poll
what: each poll with a playhead clip and source time rebuilds the `.txt` (or `.en`) element's innerHTML with the current word wrapped, even when the word index is the same as last poll, and finds the card with `CARDS.find` (O(n)) each time.
cost: 1.6 times a second while Resolve's playhead is parked on a word: one text subtree replaced, its layout invalidated, its style recomputed, in a 500-card list. Estimated well under 1 ms a tick on a desktop; it is a re-layout nobody needs and it also defeats text selection inside that card.
evidence: read only; no `res` comparison against the last highlighted index before the innerHTML write (line 852).
fix: remember the last (uid, word index) and return early when unchanged; use `cardEl`'s element dataset or a uid->card map instead of `CARDS.find`.

title: flip() interleaves layout reads with style writes over every card near the viewport
what: the loop reads `c.offsetTop` and `getBoundingClientRect()` for each card and, for a moved one, writes `style.transition` / `style.transform` before reading the next card, so each later read forces a style (and layout-validity) pass. A delete or a move near the top shifts every card below, so every card within three screens is written.
cost: per confirmed delete / move / insert: estimated 30-60 forced style passes (the number of cards in the 3-screen window), each small; at CPU x4 on a phone this is a few ms of the confirm's paint. The ripple-trim path that moves nothing pays nothing.
evidence: read only (my probe's one-card text change moved no card, so it did not exercise this).
ledger: related to the 2026-09-03 FLIP limit (FLIP_MS) - this is the remaining read/write interleave, not the old 373-card transition
fix: two passes - collect (card, dy, top) for all cards first, then write all transforms - same visual result.

title: Two `function oflAutoOn()` in one script: the app-only "keep what is open" runs in every desktop and Android browser
where: MulticamPipeline `multicam_pipeline/cards/page/15-offline.js:2741` (apps' keep) and `:3237` (snapshot autosave toggle); caller `:2746`
what: The page is one classic `<script>` (golden page.html: one `<script>` at 3954, closing at 32311), so the second declaration of `oflAutoOn` (the CR-211 snapshot toggle: true on every non-iOS browser) replaces the first (`oflInApp() && cards_auto_keep !== 'off'`). `oflAutoKeep` therefore runs in every Chrome/Edge/Firefox/Android browser on the dashboard: 4 s after boot it probes, fetches the manifest, ticks EVERY referenced clip's audio (and, on a non-touch screen, every video proxy via `oflManifest`'s default) and calls `oflDownload({auto:true})`, then repeats every 10 minutes. Inside the app, the settings switch `cards_auto_keep = 'off'` is ignored.
cost: An editor opens a cut list in desktop Chrome, never asks for offline: the tab silently downloads the whole cut list's audio + 480p proxies into Cache Storage (hundreds of MB to several GB per episode, estimated: Opus ~29 MB/h, WAV ~345 MB/h mono, proxies ~0.5 GB/h), creates an offline copy nobody asked for (so the seam, `oflTimed`, verdict flips and tracking - the CR-194/CR-206 machinery - become live on that desktop), calls `navigator.storage.persist()` (Firefox shows a permission prompt), and every 10 min re-pulls state + words + every vault transcript (estimated 3-5 MB per tab per cycle). Each new cut list opened adds a copy that is never removed (see -4). Disk fill on a laptop over weeks; NAS egress per open tab.
evidence: `autoon_probe.js`: desktop browser on the dashboard `oflInApp()=false`, `oflAutoOn()=true`; in the app with `cards_auto_keep=off`, `oflAutoOn()=true` (expected false). Both declarations are in `tests/golden/page.html:24735` and `:25231`. Keep landed 2026-10-22..28 (8fdc887), after the snapshot toggle (2026-09-06), so it has shipped broken since.
fix: rename the keep's predicate (`oflKeepOn`) and its caller; add a unit assertion that the page has no duplicate top-level function names (a regex over the assembled page in `test_page_golden.py`). Must not change the snapshot toggle's behaviour.

title: The automatic keep re-downloads every video proxy every ten minutes
what: In `oflDownload`, peaks and audio are skipped when `held(...)` (same identity already in hand, auto mode); the video line has no `held` check, and `oflStore` fetches with `cache:'reload'` + `X-Cards-Fresh`, bypassing both the HTTP cache and the worker.
cost: Every 10 min, per open page with a copy and proxies picked (default on any non-touch screen; in every desktop browser because of -1; in the Windows app always), every proxy is re-fetched whole from the NAS and re-put into Cache Storage (and, in the app, re-written to `Documents\Timeline Cards\...\Video`). A montage of 24 clips at ~20 MB each = ~480 MB per 10 min = ~2.9 GB/hour per tab (estimated).
evidence: read: `if(c.video&&OFLPICKV[c.mp])jobs.push(...)` vs `if(c.audio&&OFLPICK[c.mp]&&!held('audio',c,c.audio))`.
fix: add `&&!held('video',c,c.video)` (OFLMEDIX already records `video/<mp>` identities in `oflStore`).

title: Updating one episode's worker deletes every other episode's offline shell
what: Each episode registers its own worker (scope `/cards/p/<slug>/`) but the shell cache name is `cards-shell-<VER>` with VER = the page code hash, identical for every episode, so all episodes' shells share one cache. On a deploy, the first episode opened online installs the new worker, whose `activate` deletes every `cards-shell-*` but its own - including the old-VER cache holding every other episode's shell. Those episodes' (still old) workers then find nothing in `cachedShell()`, and the dashboard's `CARDS_SW.savedEpisodes()` stops listing them.
cost: Every Cards deploy (several a week historically). Phone holds offline copies of episodes A and B; after a deploy the editor opens A once online, boards a plane, launches B: no shell, navigation fails, and the landing's "Episodes this phone can open offline" omits B. This is exactly the 2026-10-11 ask ("you should be able to launch any project file which has been downloaded"). The queue survives in IndexedDB, so no data loss.
evidence: read; `render_sw` substitutes `page_version()` with no scope; activate filter is `n.indexOf('cards-shell-')===0 && n!==SHELL`.
ledger: related to the 2026-10-11 offline front door (cards_landing.py CARDS_SW)
fix: name the cache per scope (`'cards-shell-' + VER + '-' + <hash of registration.scope>`) and on activate delete only caches with this scope's suffix; keep the `cards-shell-` prefix so `savedEpisodes()` still finds them.

title: Downloaded media is never evicted: [ REMOVE ] orphans it while any other copy exists, and old copies pile up
what: IndexedDB `cards-offline` and Cache `cards-media` are per ORIGIN, shared by every episode under `/cards/p/*`. `oflRemove` deletes a copy's IDB rows but deletes media only when `OFLIX` becomes empty ("the media goes when the last copy does"), so removing episode A while episode B has a copy leaves all of A's audio and proxies in the cache with nothing pointing at them. `oflMediaCheck` only walks the current copy's `OFLMEDIX`, so a clip cut out of the list also stays. Copies themselves are never aged out (state ~600 KB + words + every vault transcript each).
cost: one episode's media is hundreds of MB to GBs (estimated above); each removal-with-others-present strands all of it, invisibly (the panel's sizes come from the index row, so the "used" figure the editor sees does not show it except via `storage.estimate`). With -1, every cut list opened in a desktop browser becomes such a copy.
evidence: read; comment at 3037 states the rule; media keys are `scope + offline-media/<kind>/<mp>`.
fix: on remove, delete the media keys this copy's `media` row names unless another copy's `media` row names the same key (reference count over the index's rows), and in `oflMediaCheck` drop cached keys under this scope that no copy references. Must keep "two cut lists of one episode share one copy of the audio".

title: A quota failure while queuing an offline edit is swallowed and the edit is reported as made
what: `oflSaveQueue` ends in `.catch(()=>null)`, `oflSaveState` likewise, and `oflQueueEdit` chains `.catch(()=>null)` before answering `{ok:true}` with the applied state. A `QuotaExceededError` (or any IDB failure) leaves the edit only in memory; nothing tells the editor, and the badge counts it.
cost: phone near its quota (the download refuses only when the pick exceeds free space, so a copy can leave very little headroom; media written by -1/-2 consumes it) -> offline edits all "work" -> tab reload or OS killing the PWA loses every one of them. The CR-211 rescue file is the only belt, and it is off by default on iOS.
evidence: read.
fix: let `oflSaveQueue` reject, and in `oflQueueEdit` on rejection take the edit back off `OFLQ`/`OFLSTATE` and answer `{ok:false,error:'this device is out of room: ...'}`; also say it in the panel.

title: Search answer cache in localStorage is per episode root and never pruned across roots, on the dashboard's shared origin
what: `cards_tsans:<ROOT>` keeps up to 24 answers of up to 160,000 chars each (3.84 M chars, ~7.7 MB of UTF-16) per root, and the root set only grows. localStorage is ~5 M chars per origin, and the origin is the whole CC Sync dashboard. The retry on a quota error only trims this root's own rows; every other writer (`cards_windows` registry every 2 s, `cards_force_offline`, `cards_session_expires`, `cards_offline_last`, the dashboard's own keys) fails silently once the origin is full. Each save also parses and re-stringifies the whole row set synchronously.
cost: two or three episodes with a few dozen large searches each -> origin full -> pop-out claims (17-windows.js) stop working, the offline-by-choice switch does not persist, the sign-in expiry warning loses its value.
evidence: read; answer sizes not measured (no live server), so the time to full is estimated.
fix: one global LRU across roots (cap total chars, e.g. 1 M), or move the answers to the existing IndexedDB store.

title: Every offline edit rewrites the whole queue and the whole state
where: MulticamPipeline `multicam_pipeline/cards/page/15-offline.js:396-420`, `:2092`; the replay calls `oflSaveQueue` per landed edit (`:2365`, `:2399`)
what: the queue (reorders carry the whole uid list twice) is written whole per edit, and the ~600 KB state beside it, so a day offline is O(n^2) bytes into IndexedDB.
cost: measured serialisation of the queue: 407 KB at 71 edits, 1.77 MB at 300, 3.5 MB at 600; cumulative bytes written by the queue alone 258 MB (300 edits) / 1.04 GB (600 edits), plus 600 KB of state per edit (180-360 MB). Serialise CPU is small (1 s total at 600); the cost is phone flash writes and IDB commit latency per edit.
evidence: `queue_probe.js` (v8.serialize, the IDB serializer).
ledger: related to CR-211 / CR-274 (snapshot packing solved the same lists for the file, not for IDB)
fix: store one row per edit (`q:<id>`) plus an order row, or reuse `oflSnapPack`'s list table in the stored form; write the state on the existing 2 s trailing timer rather than per edit.

title: In the apps every kept clip is stored twice on the device
where: MulticamPipeline `multicam_pipeline/cards/page/15-offline.js:2783-2815`; `docs/NATIVE-APPS.md` 4c ("a kept clip is on disk twice")
what: in the Windows/Android app the local server already writes the clip to the projects folder and answers it "before the network and whatever the verdict", yet `oflStore` also puts the full blob in Cache Storage (after materialising it with `answer.blob()`).
cost: doubles on-device media (hundreds of MB to GBs per episode, estimated); on Android that is the scarce resource.
evidence: doc says so; code read.
ledger: new (documented trade-off, cheaper way to keep the same guarantee)
fix: when `oflInApp()` and the keep header was sent, record identity in `OFLMEDIX` without `cache.put`, and have `oflMediaCheck` ask the local server whether it holds the file instead of `cache.match`. Elsewhere, `cache.put(key, new Response(answer.body, {headers}))` streams instead of holding the whole file as a Blob.

title: The shortening duck stacks `timeupdate` listeners and cuts the next duck short
what: each `shDuck` adds a `timeupdate` listener on the one shared `SHDUCK` element, removed only when `currentTime >= stop`. A second seam crossed before the first duck ends (different `in_s`, often a different clip) leaves the first listener live; if the new start is at or past the old `stop`, the old listener pauses the new duck on its first `timeupdate`. A duck that never reaches its stop (paused by `winApplyPlaying`, a failed play) leaves its listener for ever.
cost: scrubbing across two seams within half a second: the second removed block is barely heard. Listener count grows by one per interrupted duck for the page's life.
evidence: read.
fix: keep the tick in a module variable and remove the previous one before adding a new one.

title: The Windows app installs an unsigned .exe from a vault folder any editor can write
confidence: CONFIRMED (by reading both sides; not exercised)
what: [ CHECK FOR UPDATE ] downloads the file `latest.json` names from `<vault>/Apps/Timeline Cards/` (served by cards_app.py) and runs it with `spawn(file, ['/S', '--force-run'])`. The only check is a sha256 that comes from the SAME latest.json, and it is optional (`if (mine.sha256 && ...)`; Android likewise skips an empty one). There is no Authenticode check and no signature over latest.json.
cost: anyone who can write that vault folder (every editing PC maps the vault as X:, and the dashboard container holds it rw) replaces the exe and latest.json; the next editor to press INSTALL silently runs that binary with their own rights. CC Sync's own upgrade channel was made signed on 2026-08-17 for exactly this reason; this is a second, unsigned channel beside it. Android is protected by the platform's same-signing-key rule, Windows is not.
evidence: proxy.js:466 `if (mine.sha256 && sha !== ...)`; main.js:160 spawns the downloaded file silently; publish.ps1 writes sha256 into the same latest.json beside the binary; cards_app.py serves any .exe/.apk latest.json names.
fix: sign latest.json with an offline key (reuse the shape of ccsync's release_key.py) and bake the public key into the app; refuse an entry with no sha256 or a bad signature. Must not break the Android path, which can keep relying on the APK signature as well.
