fix: a priority on `run()` (interactive / normal / background) and let background runs take at most N-1 slots, so one slot is always free for a chat turn or a `now`; or cap shorten's fan-out at `maxConcurrent - 1`. Must keep the global cap and the cost budget.

title: Shorten's model calls cannot be cancelled: a closed tab keeps opus running for up to 15 minutes per call
where: features/shorten/server.ts:293-302 (`call`, no `signal`), :347-399, :426-504; no `/api/shorten/stop` route; shorten/client.ts has no abort
what: every shorten pass (structure, words, readback, scores) calls the runner with no AbortSignal and the runner's default 900 s timeout. Nothing in the route watches `res.on('close')` (chat and align `now` do).
cost: a whole-cut shorten is ~2 opus calls (words + readback) per section, 4 sections at a time: 10-20 sections = 20-40 thinking opus calls. Reloading the page or navigating away leaves all of them running and paid for, occupying the shared runner's 4 slots (finding 5) for their duration; the results are written to the record nobody is reading.
evidence: read.
fix: an AbortController per request, aborted on `res.on('close')` when not `writableEnded` (the chat route's pattern), threaded into `call()`; the page's "close the review" can also post a stop. Must keep: a section that fails leaves its row untouched with its error (already the catch path).

title: Pinned Python workers keep a per-episode corpus and translation stores with no bound
where: features/chat/bridge.py:207-238 (`CORPORA`, root -> whole corpus text + refs); features/translate/bridge.py:65-66 (`STORES`, `DRAFTS` per Script Docs dir); features/chat/server.ts:369-386
what: `CORPORA` keeps every episode's full transcript corpus (all chunks, every block ref) for the worker's life; `STORES`/`DRAFTS` keep each episode's `card_translations.json` / `gt_translations.json` loaded. Separately, every `GET /api/chat/state` (each panel open, cut-list switch, model change) ships the whole corpus over the pipe and `JSON.parse`s it on the Node event loop only to report counts.
cost: estimated ~1M characters per episode corpus (10 interviews x 90k chars) -> ~2-3 MB of Python strings per episode in the chat worker; ~100 episodes visited over weeks = ~200-300 MB that only a worker restart frees. The state call costs a ~3 MB JSON parse (~10-20 ms estimated) per panel open.
evidence: read; `ENGINES` beside them are capped (`ENGINE_KEEP`, `ENGINE_MAX`), these are not.
fix: cap `CORPORA`, `STORES`, `DRAFTS` (e.g. 8 episodes, oldest out; a store reloads from its file). Add a `corpus_info` bridge command that returns the counts and hash without `chunks`, for `/api/chat/state`.

title: Shorten's record cache grows per cut list
what: `mem` holds every cut list's record (up to 8 passes, each with suggestions carrying `source.words` arrays) and `queue` holds each key's last update promise (its resolved value included) for the server's life; the scores map beside it is capped at 32, these are not.
cost: estimated 100 KB-1 MB per shortened cut list; ~100s of cut lists over weeks = tens of MB. Small, but unbounded.
evidence: read.
fix: the same 32-entry LRU the scores use, and delete the `queue` entry when its promise is the last one (as align's `#writeClip` does).

title: Every stored alignment re-reads, re-parses and rewrites the whole clip sidecar
what: per record (not per batch): `readFile` + `JSON.parse` of the clip file for the q3-k4 merge, then `JSON.stringify` + atomic write of the whole file. A batch of 4 answers = 4 full read/parse/stringify/write cycles of the same file; all synchronous parse/stringify on the event loop that carries every user's WebSocket.
cost: measured ~10 ms parse+stringify for an 875 KB synthetic file (the translate route's comment puts real ones at 100-550 KB per interview, up to 5000 records); background alignment of an interview = hundreds of records = seconds of event-loop time in 10 ms pieces, plus one fsync'd rewrite each.
evidence: node probe `parse+stringify ms 9.9`.
ledger: related to q3-k4 (the merge is correct; only its granularity costs)
fix: store a run's records in one `#store` call per clip (merge once, write once). Keep the merge.

title: Every debounced .cut.md rewrite parses the whole file twice, copies it to .bak and fsyncs four times, all on the one event loop
what: After each saved edit (150 ms debounce) the store renders the whole head (render already re-parses its output to verify it), then parses the text again only for its layout, writes head.json twice, a .tmp and a .bak copy, with four fsyncs, synchronously on the Node thread that serves sockets and media.
cost: Measured ~43 ms of blocked event loop per write at 1,536 cuts (render 26.6 + second parse 14.6 + hashes 1.9), ~15 ms at 621 cuts; up to ~5-6 writes/s during continuous editing = ~20-25% of a core and ~1.6 MB + 4 fsyncs per write into the vault dataset. The second parse is about a third of the CPU and pure repetition.
evidence: probe.ts on scratch copies of core/ and cutmd/ against fixture cut lists (FF5 Framing Formosa E1 V1, Reproductive Rights V5); render.ts line 52 and store.ts line 831.
fix: Return the verification parse's layout from renderForWrite and drop the second parse; consider a longer debounce under continuous editing and a rate-limited .bak copy. Keep the preserving writer's check, diskIsOurs before rename, and the head.json writing markers.

title: /cards and /cards/edit both edit the same vault .cut.md files with no shared lock during the beside phase
where: ccsync dashboard/src/ccsync_dashboard/cards_edit.py:287-289 (--write on the old page's vault); editor README.md 'Pointing it at the real vault'; editor server/sync/store.ts:921-986; MulticamPipeline cards/project_engine.py:1730-1800
what: Both editors run live on one vault, each believing it owns the file; the new editor's .tcards lock is invisible to the old engine, and each side merges the other's writes as an external edit. The editor's own README says not to do this.
cost: A new-editor write landing between the old engine's _moved check and its os.replace is overwritten; the new editor then diffs the old engine's file against what it wrote and emits ops that undo its own acked edits. The window is milliseconds but the new editor writes every ~150 ms while editing. Even without the race, every new-editor write makes the old engine reload and re-slice the whole list.
evidence: Code read on both sides; no cross-editor lock or open-elsewhere signal exists. Not reproduced live.
fix: Have the old engine go read-only on a cut list whose .tcards lock is held and beating (and the new editor note when the old page wrote the file), or run /cards/edit on a working copy until the flip. Keep the Obsidian-merge path.

title: The projects list walks the vault four folders deep on every request, uncached
what: Every /api/projects runs readdir on every non-hidden folder to depth 4 under TC_VAULT plus a stat per cut list; only the per-file peek is cached.
cost: Estimated ~1,000-3,000 readdir calls per sheet open at ~100 episodes (tens to hundreds of ms warm, seconds cold on the NAS pool), linear in vault size (~5x at 500 projects). On demand only.
evidence: Code read; not timed against the real vault.
fix: Cache the key list ~30 s and invalidate on the editor's own create/rename/duplicate. New cut lists from the old page must still appear within the TTL.

title: Each cut list keeps up to 100 old log segments, three full snapshots, a .bak and an unpruned quarantine inside the vault
what: 100 segments (~20,000 ops) before the oldest kept snapshot are retained beyond what recovery needs; quarantine copies of the whole file are written on unreadable external edits and torn writes and never deleted.
cost: Estimated ~8-15 MB per actively edited cut list (snapshot measured at 799,342 bytes for 1,536 cuts), 1-4 GB of .tcards across 100-300 edited lists, churned by hourly ZFS snapshots; quarantine grows per incident.
evidence: Retention constants and prune() as cited; snapshot size from probe.ts.
fix: Lower keepOldSegments (enough to cover dedupeWindow for findInLog) and cap quarantine by count or age.

title: New log segments and renamed snapshots / head.json are not followed by a directory fsync
what: Acks wait for the segment file's fsync, but the directory entry of a segment created at the last roll (and snapshot renames) is never synced.
cost: Power loss or kernel crash only, up to 200 acked ops in a fresh segment; unlikely on ZFS, exposed on ext4/Windows standalone runs. SIGKILL loses nothing.
evidence: Code read; not reproduced.
fix: fsync the log and snap directories after creating a segment and after each rename (skip where unsupported); one extra fsync per 200 ops.

title: Every thread that reads the ledger leaks a SQLite connection for the life of the process
where: footage-sorter footage_sorter/ledger.py:342-351 (`_rd`), callers ledger.py:635 (`_decide_scans`), 1444 (`batch_summaries`), engine.py:767 (`computers`), autobackup.py:67/147
what: `_rd()` opens one reader connection per thread (thread-local) and appends it to `self._readers`, which is only closed in `close()`. The list keeps every connection alive after its thread dies. In the dashboard the sync routes run on anyio worker threads, which exit after 10 s idle and are replaced; the engine also starts a new thread per event (`sorter-ledger-sums` on every ledger/clips change a page notices, `sorter-leaves-now`, `sorter-after-ingest`, `sorter-scan`, `sorter-move-*`, `sorter-ledger-nas`). Each of those that touches the ledger adds a connection that is never freed.
cost: companions post `/sorter/agent/volumes` every 5 min per machine (`_decide_scans` reads through `_rd`); with requests spaced over 10 s apart most land on a fresh worker thread, so about 12/h/machine = ~1,150 connections/day at 4 machines, ~6,000/day at 20 (estimated). Each holds a file descriptor for ledger.db (plus WAL index mapping) and its own page cache (up to 2 MB once it has served a `batch_summaries`-sized read). Weeks of uptime = tens of thousands of fds and hundreds of MB in the dashboard's one process.
evidence: probe (1): 500 threads -> 500 live connections retained; anyio `_backends/_asyncio.py:982 MAX_IDLE_TIME = 10`.
fix: open a short-lived read connection per call (`with closing(sqlite3.connect(...))`, ~0.1 ms) or a small bounded pool, and drop the `_readers` list; or key the thread-local on a `weakref.finalize(threading.current_thread(), c.close)`. Must keep `query_only` and WAL readers.

title: A move run that raises leaves the plan "moving" forever, with no reconcile and no rescan
what: the thread body has no try/except. `Mover.execute` only catches errors inside the per-entry rename; the folder creation loop (`os.makedirs(f)` for every planned folder), the `os.stat(dst)` in the carried check, and `verify()`'s `os.stat(dst)` all raise straight out. The thread dies with `m["state"] == "moving"`, so the page shows a run in progress forever, `execute` of that plan answers 409, `reconcile_moves()` (which sets `fulfilledAt` and updates the catalog from the journal) and the follow-up scan never run.
cost: permission denied creating a folder under Projects (the deploy notes already show the container cannot read `homes/*`; any dataset ACL change does the same), disk full, or a file vanishing between `lexists` and `stat` -> the admin sees "moving" with no error, and renames that did happen before the failure are not reflected in the manifest until some later scan. No footage is lost (the journal is written per entry), but nobody is told and the state machine is wedged.
evidence: read; `run()` lines 1438-1450 and the unguarded calls named above.
fix: wrap `run()` in try/except/finally: on exception set `state = "failed"`, record the error in `m["result"]`, and in `finally` always `reconcile_moves()` under the lock and start the scan. Move the folder creation inside the guarded section of `execute` so it returns `{"ok": False, ...}` like a failed rename.

title: The rescan after a move is silently skipped when a scan is already running
what: after a move, `start_scan(wait=False)` returns `{"running": True}` without queueing anything if a scan is in flight (an earlier manual scan, or `after_ingest`'s). That scan started before or during the renames, so the clips it stores carry pre-move paths, and no scan follows to correct them.
cost: admin presses Scan, then executes a move while it runs -> clips list shows moved clips at their old Temp Transfer paths until someone scans again; the next plan for those clips is blocked with "source missing". Nothing moves wrongly (dry-run catches it), but the page is wrong and a second plan fails.
evidence: read.
fix: keep a "rescan requested" flag that `run_scan`'s `finally` honours (one more pass when it was set during the run).

title: Two concurrent Execute presses on one plan: the loser overwrites the winner's state and starts a scan mid-move
what: the `state == "dry-run"` check and the set to `"moving"` are not under any lock, and both request threads share the same `m` dict. The mover's own `_exec_lock` is non-blocking, so the second run returns `refused: another move is running`; its thread then sets `m["state"] = "refused"`, runs `reconcile_moves()` and starts a scan while the first run is still renaming. When the first finishes it overwrites the state again.
cost: double-click or two admins -> the page reports "refused" for a move that is running, and a scan walks the tree half-moved (see sorter-py-3). The renames themselves stay safe (NOREPLACE, one executor).
evidence: read; window is the GIL gap between two threadpool requests, small but real on a double-click.
fix: do the check-and-set under `self.lock` and refuse the second press with 409 before starting a thread.

title: Thumbnail workers block on the background semaphore while holding a popped job: interactive requests wait behind the backfill
what: 6 workers, background gate `min(4, max(2, cpu//2))`. A worker pops the head of the heap and only THEN acquires the gate. With only LOW (backfill) work queued, all 6 workers pop LOW jobs: 4 run ffmpeg and 2 sit blocked in `gate.acquire()`. A HIGH request (someone hovering or scrolling) is at the head of the heap but no worker is free to pop it until one of the 4 ffmpeg runs ends.
cost: the backfill after a STRIP_VERSION bump or a big ingest is ~21k-33k jobs (hours, per the code's own note). For its whole duration every cold thumbnail/strip a person asks for waits for the next ffmpeg to finish: strips of big proxies take 3.5 s (measured in the code comment), up to the 45 s timeout; the web waits 10 s (thumb) / 20 s (strip) and then answers 404 "none" with a 5-minute cache header, so the grid shows blanks for 5 minutes.
evidence: read; the design intent ("A thumbnail somebody is looking at jumps the queue") is defeated because no worker is reserved for HIGH.
fix: acquire the gate before popping a LOW job (or have LOW workers take the gate non-blocking and leave the item if none is free), so at least `workers - background` threads are always idle for HIGH work.

title: Backfill ffmpeg runs unthrottled inside the dashboard container (no -threads, no nice), for hours after any STRIP_VERSION bump
what: each of up to 4 concurrent ffmpeg processes uses ffmpeg's default thread count (all cores) and normal priority. A STRIP_VERSION bump deletes every old strip at the next backfill (`_drop_old_strips`) and re-queues every video clip (~25k-33k at today's 33,022 masters), so the NAS decodes for hours at full CPU next to SMB/Syncthing serving editors and the dashboard's own event loop. The old strips (correct for files under 50 MB) are deleted before replacements exist, so hover scrubbing is blank for most clips until the backfill reaches them.
cost: estimated 25k strips x 0.5-3.5 s / 4 parallel = 1-6 h of saturated CPU per bump; repeats on every future bump.
evidence: read; strip timing from the module's own measurements.
fix: add `-threads 1` (or 2) to LOW-priority runs and start them with `os.nice(10)`/`preexec_fn`; delete an old-version strip only when its replacement is written, not all up front.

title: Idle cost: the whole Projects tree is re-listed every 60 s, and the leaf refresh does disk I/O under the engine lock every 30 s
what: `refresh_tree` runs `read_dest_tree(destRoot, depth 8)` every 60 s forever: one `scandir` per directory down to depth 8 (every file name in each directory is read even though only directories are kept), then `json.dumps` + sha1 of the whole tree. `refresh_leaves` runs every 30 s and, when time folders are on, calls `assigned_dest_abs_list` WHILE HOLDING `self.lock`; that calls `canonical_dest` once per unfulfilled assignment (not per distinct dest), and each call does a sorted `scandir` of every path segment.
cost: today's pool scan saw 77,727 files under /pool; Projects at depth 8 is most of them, so ~1,440 full-tree listings/day (estimated tens of thousands of dirents and a few hundred ms CPU each). At 500 projects / 500k files the walk is ~7x larger and still every minute. The leaf refresh with e.g. 2,000 pending assignments x 4 segments = 8,000 `scandir`s every 30 s inside the lock that every edit, `/api/state` build and `/api/desttree` needs.
evidence: read; cadences from `start()` lines 297-298. Not timed on the pool (rule: no NAS access).
fix: walk only on demand plus a cheap change check (root mtimes of the first two levels, or after a move/scan/ingest, which already call `refresh_tree`), lengthen the timer to ~10 min; in `assigned_dest_abs_list` dedupe the sanitised dests before `canonical_dest` and pass a shared `seen`, and take the lock only to copy the manifest's dests.

title: /api/desttree: the full tree deep-copied under the engine lock and re-sent every 15 s per open tab, no ETag
what: every open sorter tab polls `api/desttree` every 15 s. Each call holds `self.lock` while it `copy.deepcopy`s the whole destination tree and merges planned folders, then sends the full JSON with `no-store`; the browser computes a signature and usually throws it away. The other big bodies (`/api/state`, `/api/clips`, `/api/dest/*`) already have versioned ETags and 304s; this one does not, though `v["dests"]` and `v["manifest"]` exist.
cost: 4 tabs = 16 deep copies and full serialisations per minute of a tree with thousands of nodes (estimated 10-100 ms each), each blocking edits for its duration; at 20 editors with the page open, 80/min.
evidence: read both sides.
fix: serve it through the existing `Served`/ETag path keyed on `(v["dests"], v["manifest"])`, so an unchanged tree is a 304 with no copy.

title: The catalog (25 MB) is rewritten and fsynced at least twice per scan even when nothing changed
what: `reconcile_journal` sets `dirty = True` unconditionally, even when the journal had no new bytes; `link_scan`/`set_location` stamp `seenAt = now` on every location, so every scan dirties every linked entry. `run_scan` therefore saves the catalog in `reconcile_moves` and again in `link_staging_scan`, both under `self.lock`, and `plan_moves` saves it again via `_link_plan_clips`.
cost: per scan: clips.json (32 MB) + 2 x catalog.json (25.7 MB on creator-1's copy) written with fsync = ~83 MB, plus the json.dumps of the catalog (~0.1 s each per the module's comment) inside the lock. Scans run on demand, after every ingest and after every move. Also fills the nightly `state-<day>` backup copies with a new catalog every day.
evidence: read; file sizes from E:\Projects\Editing\footage-sorter\data.
fix: set `dirty` in `reconcile_journal` only when the offset moved or a location changed; do not dirty on a `seenAt`-only refresh (or keep `seenAt` out of the persisted document and update it once per scan); save once at the end of `run_scan`.

title: Move plans accumulate forever, in memory and on disk, and every scan walks all of them
what: every Plan press (including blocked plans and previews) stores the full plan (all entries) in `self.moves` and in `data/moves/<id>.json`; nothing removes either. `reconcile_moves` (every scan, every move end, the reconcile route) concatenates the entries of every plan ever made into `plan_entries` and walks them again in `_executed_entries`; `/api/moves` sorts and returns all of them.
cost: a plan of all pending assignments is thousands of entries (~400 B each); tens of plans a day over weeks of uptime = tens to hundreds of MB resident and a growing per-scan loop. Memory is reset only by a restart; the disk files never are.
evidence: read.
fix: keep only the newest N plans (or those not in a terminal state from the last 24 h) in memory, and prune `moves/*.json` older than 30 days; `_withheld_entries` already carries what restart-safety needs.

title: The thumbnail and strip cache has no cap and no pruning
what: thumbnails and strips are keyed by recording and never deleted except old-version strips. Clips that leave the library (deleted, archived, cards dismissed) keep theirs.
cost: estimated ~20 KB thumbs + 15-61 KB strip per video clip: ~2 GB at today's ~36k clips, ~9 GB at 150k clips (500k files), on the apps dataset that also holds the dashboard's DB.
evidence: read.
fix: in `backfill`, which already lists both folders, remove files whose key is in no current clip and no catalog entry (older than N days, through `guard.remove`).

title: The scan's content memo is in memory only: every restart (every deploy) re-runs ~2,264 ffprobes and ~7,600 XML/WAV reads
what: `_scan_memo` caches ffprobe creation times, Sony XML and WAV headers by (path, size, mtime) but lives only in the process. The previous scan's results are already on disk in clips.json (per-clip `recordedAt`, `durationSec`, `umid`, with file sizes and mtimes).
cost: the first scan after each container restart spawns ~2,264 ffprobe processes (number from the module's own comment) over the pool; estimated 1-3 min of extra scan time and process churn per restart, scaling with the library.
evidence: read.
fix: seed the memo at load from clips.json (key the master's path/size/mtime to the stored values), or persist the memo beside clips.json.

title: Any ledger write makes every open page re-download and re-adopt the whole clip list
what: Any change of ledger.version triggers changed(), which refetches the clip views; ledger.version bumps on every committed transaction and the clips ETag includes _sum_gen, which increments on every summary rebuild even when no copy count changed, so the conditional GET never 304s after a write.
cost: During a drive scan or backup: every 30 s, or every 2 s with the Backups panel open, a full refetch: 2.7 MB gzip / 25 MB raw with the destination loaded, ~60 ms parse+index (node) plus dupMarks/filter/sort over 36k rows; a 30-min scan with the panel open is up to 900 refetches (~2.4 GB) for one tab.
evidence: ledger.py:322-329; engine.py:695-716 etag includes gen; ledger.js:384; probes: slim payload size, node JSON.parse timing.
ledger: related to footage-sorter docs/PERFORMANCE-PLAN.md ETag design; new
fix: Bump _sum_gen only when the built summaries differ, and refetch rows only when activity reports the summaries generation moved, not on any ledger version.

title: Destination tree polled every 15 s, uncompressed and uncached, while the server only re-reads it every 60 s
what: Each visible tab GETs api/desttree every 15 s; server refreshes the tree every 60 s (already with a sha1 sig), so 3 of 4 polls are identical. Each answer deep-copies the tree under engine.lock and is sent raw with no ETag; the client walks it to find nothing changed.
cost: 240 requests/hour/tab; tree >= 1,131 folders (lower bound), ~190 KB raw each = >= 45 MB/hour/tab and 240 deep copies under the engine lock; ~5x at 500 projects. PERFORMANCE-PLAN lists it as 'a few KB'.
evidence: Probe: folder count from local clips.json; code read.
fix: Serve desttree via serve_blob (gzip + ETag from _tree_sig + planned folders) and poll every 60 s.

title: Every assign/unassign downloads the whole manifest uncompressed and redraws every pane twice
what: The edit reply carries the whole manifest; _json never gzips and the dashboard has no GZip middleware, so it is 2.9 MB raw, not the 0.3 MB the plan assumes. afterManifestChange() runs optimistically and again on reply, each time re-rendering source tree, dest tree with coverage, events, filters, Missing checks.
cost: 100 drags in a session = ~290 MB downloaded and 200 full redraw passes; ~1.2 s per drag on a 20 Mbit/s phone link.
evidence: Probe: manifest 13,595 assignments = 2,915,125 bytes raw; no GZipMiddleware in dashboard/src.
ledger: related to footage-sorter docs/PERFORMANCE-PLAN.md 'Not changed' (whole manifest per edit); compression gap and double redraw are new
fix: gzip _json bodies above ~8 KB or reply with only changed assignments + leaves; skip the second afterManifestChange when the reply matches the optimistic state.

title: Page assets shipped uncompressed, unversioned, and with the development mock
what: 11 JS/CSS files served raw with no-cache and unversioned URLs (12 revalidations per open); dev-mock.js (41 KB, only active with ?mock=1) ships and is parsed every load.
cost: Cold load 606 KB instead of 158 KB gzip; warm load 12 round trips before scripts run.
evidence: Probe: wc/gzip of public/.
fix: Version script URLs with DEPLOYED_COMMIT and serve immutable + gzip; load dev-mock.js only with ?mock=1 or drop it from the deploy.

title: Audio tab poll keeps running in a hidden browser tab and is never cleared
what: A 30 s setInterval started on first Audio-tab visit lives forever and checks only the panel tab, not document.hidden; a backgrounded tab left on Audio refetches api/audio and rebuilds the DOM every 30 s.
cost: 120 requests/hour per forgotten tab plus full transcript re-render.
evidence: Code read; other pollers check document.hidden.
fix: Return when document.hidden and clear the interval when the tab is left.

title: Session list polled every 5 s although an event stream for it is open
what: Every visible tab GETs api/ingest/sessions every 5 s while also holding the api/ingest/events SSE open; with no card in, the answer never changes.
cost: 720 requests/hour/visible tab; with the desttree and ledger polls ~1,000 requests/hour per idle tab.
evidence: Code read.
fix: Push a sessions event over the SSE on change; keep a 30-60 s fallback poll.

title: Hover intent can queue an ffmpeg filmstrip job on the NAS for every card the pointer crosses
what: 90 ms on a card fetches api/strip/<key>; for a cold clip the server enqueues a strip job and waits up to 20 s; the fetch is never aborted on leave.
cost: Estimated: sweeping across 20 cold cards queues 20 strip jobs ahead of the one wanted; harmless once strips are backfilled (not checked).
evidence: Code read.
fix: Prefetch only existing strips (nowait 404) and enqueue generation at the 300 ms scrub start.

title: Em dashes and Node-era instructions in user-visible strings
where: footage-sorter public/app.js (~42 literals, :1935, :2412, :4102, :4524, :1179), grid.js:330-337, ingest.js (~19), calendar.js (~7), cards.js (3), audio.js (2), ledger.js (1)
what: About 81 visible string literals contain an em dash (owner rule) with no scan test covering the sorter; two messages point a NAS user at server.js and npm.
cost: Every toast/tooltip shown; a boot failure toast misdirects the operator.
evidence: grep for U+2014 inside string literals.
fix: Replace with hyphen/colon, reword the two messages, add an em-dash scan over footage-sorter/public.

title: The docs still install and start the retired tray and Node server beside the companion
what: INGEST.md set-up still says to run ingest\tray\Install.ps1, which recreates the Auto Backup Utility Startup shortcut; that tray starts node server.js and polls drives every 3 s with a WMI query per tick. README still says npm start and mover.ps1 -Execute. SORTER_DEPLOY.md retired the tray 2026-11-10 because the companion detects cards now.
cost: A machine set up from INGEST.md gets two card watchers and two TeraCopy drivers on one card, plus a second manifest writer that no longer matches /sorter; mover.ps1 moves behind the NAS sorter's ledger and catalog.
evidence: Startup and Startup (retired) .lnk targets; no scheduled task or process; doc text; DASHBOARD-MODULE-PLAN phase 3 says the Node server retires to legacy/, not done.
fix: Retired banner at the top of README/INGEST/SPEC pointing to /sorter and FIELD_BACKUP.md; move the retire-safe pieces to legacy\ with a README row.

title: lib/ and server.js cannot retire because they are the parity oracle, and that suite runs in no CI
what: 13 test_parity_*.py files run the frozen JS (last change 2026-11-01) in a Node child. That keeps about 7,200 lines of JS, express and Node on PATH as a test dependency. Neither the sorter suite nor its parity tests run in any CI.
cost: Deliberate Python changes since cut-over either break parity tests or are uncovered, and nobody sees which; retiring the JS today turns 13 test files into errors.
evidence: require lists in the drivers; git log on lib/ and server.js; ccsync ci.yml covers only test_sorter_deploy.py; no .github in footage-sorter.
fix: Record the oracle's answers once as JSON goldens, point the parity tests at them, then move server.js, lib/ and package.json to legacy\; keep tools/gen-collation.js; add tests/py to CI.

title: Duplicate decision drift: Node calls equal-size files over 64 MiB identical, Python reads every byte
what: Move-plan resolution drops a destination already holding a same-size file, or a second source to the same destination, as alreadyThere/duplicates. Node decides from size alone above 64 MiB; Python compares full contents.
cost: Only if Node runs again: two different equal-size takes, one silently left out of the move and reported redundant; purge-dupes.js builds its list from that export but its own verify refuses true mismatches.
evidence: The two functions.
fix: Retire the Node path; record the drift in the goldens so Python is not reverted.

title: TeraCopy switch drift: Node and the PS1 workers copy new files with /OverwriteDiffSize; the companion uses /SkipAll
where: footage-sorter lib/teracopy.js:75, lib/ingest/plan.js:16,279, server.js:174, ingest/tray/Config.psd1:198, ingest/tray/Common.ps1:186,349-355 vs ccsync companion/src/ccsync_companion/teracopy.py:71-74, card_copy.py:816-819
what: A file planned as copy (destination absent at plan time) goes to TeraCopy with /OverwriteDiffSize, so a different-size file that lands at that name before the job runs (a second card's C0001.MP4) is overwritten. The companion uses /SkipAll for copies. In the PS1 path Invoke-TeraCopy also returns 0 on presence+size when the History DB is unreadable (the JS returns 12), and Get-TeraCopyStatus matches by destination and time without the source list.
cost: Dead on creator-1; live again if the tray is reinstalled with LegacyWorkers = $true (the shipped default) and the server unreachable.
evidence: Lines cited.
fix: Retire ingest/tray, lib/ingest and lib/teracopy.js; the companion twin is correct.

title: The October ledger Worker still takes writes after the cut-over to ledger.db
what: The plan says the Worker stays read-only for a month, but nothing enforces it; the razer field tools were its writers. A copy written to D1 after 2026-11-10 reaches ledger.db only on a manual re-import, and the daily cron email keeps reporting from D1.
cost: Pessimistic not-at-home / safe-to-format for such cards, two disagreeing not-at-home lists, and D1 daily limits shared with /cards and /expenses stay at risk.
evidence: Route table and auth read; razer not checked under the rules.
fix: Deploy with a READ_ONLY flag that 405s POST/PUT and stop the cron, or set the delete date; confirm nothing on razer points at /backups/api.

title: 24 MB of machine state tracked in git and pushed to GitHub; 636 MB of dead local state
where: footage-sorter data/manifest.backup-*.json, data/moveplan.*.json, data/dupes-20260819.json, data/server.out.log, data/settings.json; .gitignore
what: Manifest backups, executed move plans and a server log are committed (manifest.backup-* is not ignored); they carry every P:\ path and project/person folder names, settings.json the owner's address and calendar ids. data/ (176 MB) and cache/ (460 MB) on creator-1 are dead after the migration.
cost: About 24 MB in every clone and personal data in a GitHub repo; 636 MB stale on creator-1.
evidence: git ls-files blob sizes; du.
fix: git rm --cached those files and extend .gitignore; archive data/ and cache/ with the Node server into legacy\.

title: One cached 'is Resolve running' probe instead of a tasklist spawn behind nine doors
where: companion/src/ccsync_companion/resolve_prefs.py:143-171; callers capabilities.py:495-520, jobs_runner.py:614/682/736/758/817, broll_ingest.py:1004/1114, proxy_gen.py:705-723/925, resolve_bridge.py:640-662, app.py:4926/4993/12587, luts.py:474, resolve_prefs.py:367/462/519/572
what: Every Windows 'is Resolve up' question spawns tasklist (macOS pgrep). Three modules grew private TTL caches around it, the rest call it raw; capabilities caches everything except this field. script_server already reads the process table in-process every 3 s.
cost: Per Windows editor ~230-545 tasklist spawns/hour idle Resolve closed, ~110-245 Resolve open, ~800-1,100 while syncing (report every 5 s), +~29 per ingested clip; 202 ms wall each = 45-110 s spawn wall time per idle hour beside Resolve; 5,000-11,000 spawns/hour across 20 machines.
evidence: Grep of all callers (one spawn site, nine paths). Probe: tasklist median 202 ms vs script_server._windows_processes()+is_resolve_name median 8.5 ms over 499 processes; a cache hit is a lock + monotonic read.
ledger: consolidates comp-jobs-2, comp-media-1, comp-resolve-7; the reporter/capabilities door (60/h idle, 720/h syncing) is new
fix: Windows branch of resolve_process_state() -> Toolhelp32 snapshot (reuse script_server._windows_processes, match Resolve.exe so BPG still counts) behind ONE module-level 5 s TTL cache of the three-valued answer; same cache for pgrep on macOS. Keep fail-closed collapse, positive-sighting-only for the scripting warning, and let prefs writes ask fresh=True.

title: On a Mac, both sorter loops spawn diskutil for every mounted volume every 10 seconds
where: companion/src/ccsync_companion/sorter_cards.py:194-244 (_mac_volumes), called from sorter_cards.py current_cards (scope local) and sorter_volumes.py current_volumes (scope all); SCAN_SECONDS 10 in both; both default on
what: Two default-on loops enumerate the same volumes independently; on macOS each enumeration spawns one 'diskutil info -plist' per /Volumes entry, startup disk included, before any freshness check (RELIST_SECONDS applies after list_volumes).
cost: 2 loops x 360 ticks/h x 2-4 volumes = 1,440-2,880 diskutil spawns/hour, 35k-70k/day per Mac for weeks, ~50-150 ms each (estimated), on laptops on battery, whether or not the studio uses the sorter.
evidence: Code read of both loops and _mac_volumes; comp-field covered the Windows ctypes path only.
ledger: new (related: comp-app OUT OF TERRITORY note on default-on sorter scans; comp-field-9 Windows relist)
fix: One shared enumerator with a ~10 s cache read by both loops; on macOS cache each diskutil answer keyed on (mount path, st_dev) and re-run only for a new or changed mount; capacity/free from shutil.disk_usage. Keep the Data-volume serial rule and the busy-volume reuse.

title: The proxy geometry-verdict cache keeps every proxy path it ever saw, with no field eviction
what: Geometry verdicts are keyed by proxy path and validated by fingerprint on read, but only a tests-only function ever clears the dict; it grows with every distinct proxy examined for the life of the process.
cost: ~250-400 bytes/entry (estimated): a few MB today over weeks; 500k proxies at commercial scale (500 projects x 5k files on a base rig) ~100-200 MB in the tray process.
evidence: Code read: one writer, one clear reachable only from tests, no size check.
fix: OrderedDict LRU capped ~20,000 (a miss only re-probes, so verdicts cannot change); cap _REFUSALS generously or evict on project close so a refused proxy in play stays refused.

title: Two upload-queue threads poll every second forever, and the originals inbox lists its folder every 2 s, though all have a wake path
what: After the first upload the UploadQueue worker wakes every second to find an empty queue, though every enqueue/resume/stop sets _wake. The originals inbox iterdir()s a local folder every 2 s for a request dropped a few times a week.
cost: 120 wakeups/min plus 1,800 directory listings/hour per machine for weeks, about a third of the ~360 idle wakeups/min in the census; small CPU, but no deep idle on laptops.
evidence: Code read; every queue state change calls self._wake.set().
fix: Idle branch waits on _wake with no or a 60 s timeout; originals inbox every 10-15 s or woken via the 8899 loopback. Keep the explicit 5 s NAS-unreachable retry and stop() waking the thread.

title: Shutdown is unbounded in front and serial behind, so docker stop SIGKILLs the lifespan - including the Node editor's cut-list flush - whenever a Cards page or agent is connected
where: dashboard/deploy/run.sh:592-598 and :607 (no --timeout-graceful-shutdown); uvicorn server.py:272-302; dashboard/src/ccsync_dashboard/app.py:942-972; cards_edit.py:107 and 303-322; no stop_grace_period in the repo
what: uvicorn drains every in-flight request with no timeout BEFORE the lifespan shutdown runs (a Cards page always has a 25 s long poll; each Cards-role machine a 25 s /cards/agent/pending; abandoned media ranges run to EOF). The lifespan then joins watchdog (5 s), collector (10 s) and executor (5 s) before sending the Node editor the SIGTERM that flushes cut lists (15 s grace). Docker's SIGTERM reaches only run.sh and uvicorn.
cost: Every image deploy is a docker stop with the default 10 s grace: with one Cards page open the SIGKILL lands before the lifespan starts (no engine stop, no Node flush). With nothing connected the joins still sum to 20 s before Node is asked. On the exit-75 OTA path the same sequence is up to ~65 s of downtime before re-exec. Becomes high when /cards/edit is released.
evidence: uvicorn _wait_tasks_to_complete loops while connections exist, timeout_graceful_shutdown default None; run.sh flags read; repo-wide grep for stop_grace|stop_timeout|timeout-graceful returns nothing; app.py shutdown order read.
fix: Pass --timeout-graceful-shutdown 5 in run.sh; send Node its SIGTERM first and overlap the other stops (signal all, join after); set stop_grace_period ~40s in the compose. Keep watchdog-before-collector and executor-before-engine ordering.

title: Mount-time workers are never stopped, and on an exit-75 restart their ffmpeg/CLI children outlive the process into the next one
what: The ytdl worker/canary/nightly start in create_app and nothing stops them. Exit 75 (OTA restart, collector-watchdog recovery) ends only uvicorn; run.sh stays PID 1 and adopts orphans. The conversion ffmpeg runs at -loglevel error, writes nothing to its readerless stderr pipe, so it keeps encoding while the next process's _boot_recovery restarts the same job. Cards claude CLI children also run to completion unread.
cost: An OTA during a 1440p/2160p conversion (tens of minutes, web-ytdl-2) leaves two ffmpeg processes on the NAS CPU and an orphan writing staging files the new run also produces or sweeps. A watchdog exit-75 during a translation leaves 3-14 orphan CLIs (dash-mounts-4). Rare today, likelier at 20 editors.
evidence: Read as cited; ffmpeg progress is info-level and suppressed by -loglevel error; run.sh restart loop keeps PID 1 across exit 75. Not reproduced in a container.
fix: Start the ytdl worker from the lifespan or register a stop hook; keep Popen handles of ffmpeg/CLI children in a registry the lifespan terminates, or start them in their own process group and killpg before exiting 75. Keep ytdl boot recovery treating the job as resumable.

title: No memory limit, and every resident cache lives in the one process the fleet depends on: the OOM victim is the dashboard
where: app compose / install scripts (no mem_limit or limits in the repo); music/web/musicweb/text_encoder.py:266; b-roll and music index holders (web-broll-3, web-music-4); cards_ai.py:559
what: The music text tower (+560 MB after one search), both search indexes with 2-3x rebuild peaks, two Cards engines and the sorter catalog accumulate in uvicorn for life; the spiky consumers (CLI children, ffmpeg) are other processes in the same container. With no cgroup limit the host OOM killer picks by RSS: the uvicorn process.
cost: Busy moment today about 2.6 GB (1.4 GB in uvicorn); commercial scale about 8.8 GB (4.7 GB in uvicorn). Headroom on today's 64 GB NAS; an OOM of the fleet dashboard on an 8-16 GB appliance with ZFS ARC during a 50k-track rebuild plus a translation.
evidence: Sum of hunters' measured figures (CARDS_TWO_PROJECTS s12, web-music-3/4, web-broll-3) plus labelled estimates; grep for memory limits finds none.
ledger: related to web-music-3, web-music-4, web-broll-3, dash-mounts-4
fix: Set a container memory limit sized from the budget (about 4 GB today); evict the ONNX session after N idle minutes (reload 0.67 s); cap CLI children per dash-mounts-4. A reload failure must degrade search, never the mount.

title: One unpartitioned 40-token threadpool carries both 25 s parked long polls and every sync route, so the standing reservation grows with fleet size
where: dashboard/src/ccsync_dashboard/cards_tunnel.py:455-528; gear_ai.py:296-298; every sync route in the dashboard and broll/music/ytdl mounts; no CapacityLimiter in dashboard/src
what: All blocking work shares anyio's default 40 tokens. The Cards agent long poll parks one token and one open SQLite connection per Cards-role machine for 25 s back to back; gear photos park one each while queued; index rebuilds and provider probes hold one for seconds.
cost: At 20 Cards-role machines, 20 of 40 tokens are permanently asleep; 20 more slow holders (a gear burst, rebuilds during an ingest batch) queue /api/v1/report and every sync route with no error. Today it needs a 40-photo burst.
evidence: Census of holders from the code and territory reports; the 2026-09-18b verifier grep confirms no limiter is configured.
ledger: related to wire-5 (open, low) and dash-mounts-3
fix: Give long-hold routes their own anyio.CapacityLimiter (async def + to_thread.run_sync with that limiter) and release the get_conn connection before the hold. Keep the no-engine hold's pacing (dash-cards-1).

title: The sorter ledger opens a new SQLite connection for every short-lived thread and never closes it
where: footage-sorter footage_sorter/ledger.py:342-351 (_rd); footage_sorter/engine.py:808 (thread per ledger change), also engine.py:387,422,939,1451,1477, ledger_sources.py:227,365
what: _rd() caches a reader in threading.local but also appends it to self._readers, closed only in close(). A thread that exits loses its slot but the list keeps the connection. ledger_summaries_now starts a new thread on every ledger version change and batch_summaries calls _rd() there; scans, moves, audits and NAS/cloud listings do the same per event.
cost: One leaked connection (about 2.3 MB page cache + shm map, 2 handles) per ledger change a page sees, for the life of the dashboard process. Hundreds of MB within weeks today; days at commercial scale.
evidence: p_readers.py: 200 short-lived threads each reading a 200k-row ledger -> 200 readers, +401 handles, +466 MB RSS.
fix: Use a per-call reader (or close it in a finally) in short-lived threads, or a small fixed reader pool; make ledger_summaries_now single-flight on one long-lived worker. Keep readers separate from the writer and query_only.

title: Every ledger change makes each open page re-run two whole-table scans of copies (1.0 s + 0.7 s at 2M files); the stats scan has no covering index
what: _volume_stats groups every live row of copies (plan: SCAN copies USING INDEX copies_seq + TEMP B-TREE FOR GROUP BY). The memo lasts only until the next version bump, and each bump makes every open sorter page reload volumes and not-home.
cost: Per ledger change per process, at 2,010,000 rows: 1013 ms + 701 ms on NVMe, estimated several times that on the NAS HDD pool, each holding a threadpool worker.
evidence: p_big.py on the real Ledger schema with 2,010,000 rows and ANALYZE; p_big2.py: partial covering index copies(volume_id, role, size) WHERE live -> covering scan, 114-116 ms (9x).
fix: Add the partial covering index in a v4 migration; narrow _not_home with a partial index on (name_lc, size, volume_id) for live master/audio rows or a maintained home flag. Keep test_ledger_plans.py green.

title: The daily ledger backup holds the writer lock for the whole online backup
what: backup() runs self._w.backup(dst) in one step under _wlock, so every volume report, copy receipt and scan chunk waits. In WAL a separate read connection gives a consistent snapshot without the writer lock.
cost: Once a day: 0.9 s at 2M rows (458 MB) to local NVMe, estimated several seconds to the HDD pool, during which all ledger writes block.
evidence: Online backup of the probe DB: 0.9 s; integrity_check 2.6 s (outside the lock).
fix: Back up from a fresh query_only connection without taking _wlock. Never a file copy of the live DB or WAL.

title: Clips fetched on demand from the b-roll archive and the music library are never evicted from a remote editor's disk
what: Send to Resolve pulls the ORIGINAL clip into <local_root>/Assets/B-roll Archive/<rel> (or Assets/Music/<rel>). That folder is not synced and nothing ever deletes from it, so each remote machine converges on the whole archive the module says editors must not be made to sync.
cost: Estimated 10 inserts/week/remote editor x ~300 MB = ~13 GB/month, ~150 GB/year per remote editor (3 of 4 machines), ceiling = the archive; unreported anywhere.
evidence: broll_fetch.py header; no unlink of the archive or music rel anywhere in companion/src (grep); broll_standins.py:440 prunes ledger entries only.
fix: Record completed fetches in state/fetched_assets.json; a daily pass deletes fetched files older than 90 days that no project's media pool references per the media-tree walk the companion already does, deleting nothing when that walk cannot answer; never run where local_root is the NAS; show the total in Settings.

title: Save-point exports (.drp, tens of MB) of a project nobody edits any more are never swept
what: The 60-day sweep runs only on the write path and only in the directory of the project being journalled, so a project that stops being edited keeps its last 60 days of .drp rollback exports in ~/.ccsync/resolve_edits for ever. RESOLVE_EDIT_SAFETY.md's 'swept on the next write' is true only for a project that gets a next write.
cost: Estimated 2-6 save points per active project-day x 20-50 MB; 0.4-5 GB stranded per finished project per machine; ~10-50 GB/year per editor in HOME on the system disk, invisible to every report.
evidence: Code read: _sweep(slug) is called only from the session open; the other journal_root() readers (app.py:10200, :10220) only list.
ledger: related to comp-resolve-4 (FIXED 2026-08-21: added .drp to the sweep, kept the per-slug trigger)
fix: Run the existing _sweep over every slug directory once at startup and once a day (same 60 days, same suffixes), removing empty slug dirs; optionally keep only the newest .drp per project per day past 14 days. Undo replays the JSON journals, whose 60 days are unchanged.

title: Every force-kill of the companion leaves two 108 MB PyInstaller extraction folders in %TEMP%
where: companion/build.spec:333-352 (onefile, runtime_tmpdir=None); installer/windows_upgrade.ps1:184 (Stop-Process -Force); supervisor.py (same exe, second extraction)
what: A onefile build unpacks to %TEMP%\_MEI* and only the bootloader parent removes it. windows_upgrade.ps1, the uninstaller and Stop-Process by image name kill parent and child of both the companion and its supervisor, stranding two extraction folders per stop; nothing sweeps _MEI* folders.
cost: Measured 108,117,253 bytes per extraction x 2 per stop; the base rig runs windows_upgrade.ps1 on every ship (~10/month) = ~2.2 GB/month, ~26 GB/year on C:; 216 MB per hand install or uninstall elsewhere.
evidence: PyInstaller CArchiveReader over companion/dist/ccsync-companion.exe: 1,335 files, 108 MB (PyInstaller 6.21.0); build.spec; windows_upgrade.ps1:184; KNOWN_BUGS supervisor entry.
ledger: related to COMMERCIAL_READINESS L-list 'onefile _MEI temp' (security angle)
fix: At startup, after the single-instance slot is held, delete %TEMP%\_MEI* folders older than an hour that are not sys._MEIPASS and carry this build's marker (e.g. ccsync_lib/), skipping locked ones; same sweep at the end of windows_upgrade.ps1. Never touch other apps' or onboard.exe's extraction.

title: The APP dataset's 24 hourly + 30 daily snapshots pin the dashboard DB's rewrite churn and everything deleted from <data>, sized on a 'kilobytes per hour' assumption
what: Copy-on-write snapshots keep the old version of every block changed between snapshots. dashboard.db and its WAL are rewritten all day on default 128K records (each dirty 4 KB page pins 128 KB), and every file deleted from <data> (OTA DB copies, packages, caches, thumbnails) is held 30 more days. Nothing reports usedbysnapshots.
cost: WAL writes ~0.5-2 GB/day today (collector alone 0.48 GB/day per dash-collector-1's measurement); estimated 1-5 GB held by the 54 snapshots plus ~1 GB per OTA held 30 days; scales with machine count.
evidence: Cited hunters' WAL measurements; setup_snapshots.py docstring; no recordsize, journal_size_limit or usedbysnapshots in the tree (grep).
ledger: related to dash-db-1, dash-db-2, dash-collector-1, dash-collector-3, dash-api-5, dash-ops-2, ops-server-1
fix: Put the SQLite files in a new child dataset with recordsize=16K (installer-created, never altering the operator's existing dataset); read usedbysnapshots for the APP dataset in the collector's daily pass and show it on the health page; correct the docstring. Keep 24h/30d retention.

title: Footage Sorter keeps a full manifest copy for every day it is used, and its two journals only grow
what: save_manifest rewrites logs/manifest-YYYYMMDD.json with the whole manifest on every save (fsynced) and never prunes the daily files; manifest-ops.jsonl and move-journal.jsonl are append-only for ever. Nothing removes anything under logs/.
cost: ~2.9 MB x ~25 edit days/month = ~73 MB/month, ~0.9 GB/year on the APP dataset and its snapshots; move journal 11 MB / 39,264 lines today; estimated 3-5x at 500k files; every edit writes the manifest twice.
evidence: Code read; manifest size from docs/DASHBOARD-MODULE-PLAN.md:310; move-journal figures from sorter-py's probe.
fix: Write the daily copy only if today's is absent; keep 30 daily + one per month for 12 months, pruned at that write; rotate manifest-ops.jsonl at 10 MB keeping 3; compact move-journal.jsonl by dropping done start/done pairs older than 90 days, never an unfinished entry.

title: The NAS keeps a year of staggered Syncthing versions for every project folder, and nothing measures it
what: Every non-video file an editor replaces on the NAS keeps staggered versions for 365 days (up to ~100 per file). Deletes are already covered by ignoreDelete, so these guard only against bad overwrites; no companion or collector measures .stversions and the weekly report omits it.
cost: Estimated: a 50 MB project/graphics file saved daily for a month keeps ~55 versions = ~2.7 GB; tens of GB a year across ~100 projects on the tree dataset, further pinned by ops-server-1's pre-op snapshots.
evidence: Config read; KNOWN_BUGS ~7783 ('.stversions retention is 365 d NAS-side'); alerts.py comment.
ledger: related to KNOWN_BUGS versioning_agrees (registered, not evaluated, by design)
fix: Collector totals <tree>/**/.stversions in one bounded daily walk and reports it in the weekly mail and health page with a site threshold alert; lowering maxAge to 90 days is an owner decision once the number is known. Editor-side 30 days unchanged.

title: The old Cards page has no retirement step: ~61,000 lines and a second implementation of every Cards feature stay live after the flip
where: MulticamPipeline multicam_pipeline/cards/page/*.js (24 files, 32,741 lines), tests/*.js (44 files, 28,022 lines); ccsync docs/CARDS_EDITOR.md:161-180; editor PARITY.md:40, :291
what: The flip moves the old page to /cards/old for one release but names no step that deletes it, its JS tests, its page-only handler routes or the offline seam the native apps load. Every Cards change has two homes (32.7k JS vs 91k TS) and PARITY.md is the hand-kept ledger between them.
cost: Every Cards change x2 implementations; 28k lines of page tests in the Cards gate on every iteration. The Windows and Android apps (8,579 lines) still load the old page, so it cannot be deleted at the flip either - the apps are the hidden blocker.
evidence: git ls-files + wc -l: page 32,741; tests/*.js 28,022; editor TS 91,016 + 53,239 test lines; CARDS_EDITOR.md phase 5; PARITY.md rows 40 and 291 (the apps still load the old page).
fix: Add a phase 6 to CARDS_EDITOR.md: move the native apps to the new editor, then one release after the flip git rm cards/page/, the page tests and the page-only routes (keep /agent/* and what cards_tunnel and the companion role import), and drop the PARITY.md rows.

title: The footage sorter tracks 23.6 MB of manifest backups, move plans and logs, with real interviewee names, on GitHub, against its own .gitignore
where: footage-sorter data/manifest.backup-*.json (8), data/moveplan*.json (11), data/dupes-20260819.json, data/server.err.log, data/server.out.log; .gitignore (data/manifest.json, data/roster.json entries)
what: .gitignore keeps data/manifest.json out because it holds names of real people, yet eight timestamped full copies of it and the executed move plans are tracked and pushed to github.com/The-Creators-Club/footage-sorter; a sample carries Interviewees/<full name> paths.
cost: 23.6 MB per clone (the code is ~1 MB) and a documentary's interviewee list in a repo of a product going commercial.
evidence: git ls-files -z data | xargs -0 du -ck = 23,576 KB; git remote -v; grep of one backup for Interviewees/; .gitignore comment text.
fix: git rm --cached the backups, move plans, dupes and logs; add data/*.backup*, data/moveplan*, data/*.log to .gitignore (files stay on disk). History purge is a separate owner decision. Check SORTER_DEPLOY.md before touching episodes.json / settings.json.

title: The companion build collects all of onnxruntime: 306 .py files (3.87 MB) and 156 submodules of transformers/quantization/tools that the code never imports
where: ccsync companion/build.spec:80-93 (collect_all onnxruntime); uses: onnxruntime.InferenceSession, SessionOptions, get_available_providers only
what: collect_all defaults to include_py_files=True, so every .py under onnxruntime/ ships as a raw data file extracted on every start, and every importable submodule becomes a hidden import; 156 of 168 are exporter/optimiser tooling.
cost: ~4 MB and ~300 files of the 108 MB per-start extraction (lens-disk-3), on every editor machine, twice per start (companion + supervisor).
evidence: Companion venv, PyInstaller 6.21.0: collect_all returned 318 datas (306 .py, 3.87 MB), 168 hidden imports (156 under transformers/quantization/tools), binaries onnxruntime.dll 18.1 MB + providers_shared; grep of ccsync_companion for onnxruntime. finds the three names only.
fix: Replace collect_all with collect_dynamic_libs(onnxruntime) + hiddenimports onnxruntime, onnxruntime.capi.onnxruntime_pybind11_state, onnxruntime.capi._pybind_state + the notices file; prove with tools/scan_frozen.py and a frozen CLAP-sidecar smoke. Must not drop the DLLs.

title: ffmpeg_tools twins: the indexer's copy has no timeout on any of its ten ffmpeg/ffprobe calls, and the verbatim-twin helpers are not pinned across the two copies
what: 145 shared normalised lines. count_frames gained timeout + TimeoutExpired only in the companion; _plausible_frames (docstring: a verbatim twin) coerces with float() only in the companion. test_ffmpeg_tools.py imports the indexer for the preview flags but does not compare frames_match, _plausible_frames, parse_frame_count or count_frames_cmd.
cost: The indexer reads originals over SMB on the base rig for ~5,000-clip runs; one ffprobe stuck on a stalled read blocks its worker forever with no error. The unpinned helpers are the three-checks-each-thought-another-had-looked shape of the Reproductive Rights defect.
evidence: funcdiff.py: _plausible_frames ratio 0.40, count_frames 0.47 (diffs in scratchpad); no timeout= on any indexer subprocess.run.
fix: Give the indexer's probes PROBE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS (and encodes a duration-scaled timeout); add four assertions to test_ffmpeg_tools.py comparing the indexer's frames_match, _plausible_frames, parse_frame_count, count_frames_cmd on the same inputs. Keep frames_match exact.

title: Cards read-only guard is a second hand-kept list beside the route chain and has drifted: /api/fade writes a read-only project
what: READONLY_BLOCK lists 53 cut-changing paths against 64 POST branches. /api/fade (2026-09-15) changes the cut and is missing while its sibling /api/gain is present; ProjectEngine relies on the handler's one guard and _do_fade -> _save has no readonly check.
cost: A standalone server.py --project X --readonly session (not the dashboard mount): dragging a fade handle writes the .cut.md that was opened read-only.
evidence: Set difference of POST paths minus READONLY_BLOCK = 22 paths; only /api/fade writes the cut (set_note checks readonly itself); code paths quoted.
fix: Add /api/fade to READONLY_BLOCK and make ProjectEngine._save refuse when self.readonly. Do not refactor the handler: it retires with the old page (lens-dup-1).

title: The Cards media-job recipes are pinned against a literal, the shape audit F8 already found fails nothing when the other side moves
what: CLAUDE.md says jobs_media reproduces library_engine's argv VERBATIM; the test compares jobs_media to a hand-copied list, so a change on the Cards side fails nothing. They agree today (checked by hand).
